easy.q: How many positive factors does 2^3 × 3^2 × 5^1 have?
easy.why: Add 1 to each exponent and multiply: (a+1)(b+1)(c+1).

easy.q: What is the LCM of 12, 18 and 30?
easy.why: Take the highest power of each prime across the numbers and multiply.

easy.q: What is the units digit of 7^45?
easy.why: Units digits repeat in a cycle of 4; use n mod 4 (a remainder of 0 means the 4th place in the cycle).

easy.q: What is the remainder when 48573 is divided by 9?
easy.why: A number leaves the same remainder mod 9 as its digit sum.

easy.q: What is the LCM of 8, 20 and 36?
easy.why: Take the highest power of each prime across the numbers and multiply.

easy.q: What is the units digit of 2^63?
easy.why: Units digits repeat in a cycle of 4; use n mod 4 (a remainder of 0 means the 4th place in the cycle).

medium.q: How many zeros are there at the end of 130!?
medium.why: Zeros = number of factors of 5, counting n/5 + n/25 + n/125 + ...

medium.q: What is the remainder when 13^99 is divided by 7?
medium.why: Reduce the base mod m first, then use the repeating cycle of powers.

medium.q: The HCF of two numbers is 6 and their LCM is 180. If one number is 36, what is the other?
medium.why: Product of the two numbers = HCF × LCM.

medium.q: How many integers from 1 to 500 are divisible by 6 or 15 (or both)?
medium.why: Inclusion-exclusion: subtract the multiples of LCM counted twice.

medium.q: What is the sum of all positive factors of 2^3 × 3^2?
What is the remainder when 7^100 is divided by 6?
medium.why: Reduce the base mod m first, then use the repeating cycle of powers.

hard.q: What is the remainder when 17^101 + 19^101 is divided by 36?
hard.why: For odd n, a^n + b^n is divisible by a+b = 36, which here is a multiple of 36.

hard.q: How many factors of 2^6 × 3^4 × 5^3 are perfect squares?
hard.why: A square factor needs even exponents: choose 0,2,4,... for each prime.

hard.q: What are the last two digits of 7^123?
hard.why: Find the cycle of powers mod 100 and reduce the exponent.

hard.q: What is the highest power of 12 that divides 50! exactly?
hard.why: 12 = 2^2 × 3, so take the smaller of (power of 2)/2 and the power of 3 in n!.

hard.q: What is the sum of all odd positive factors of 2^3 × 3^2 × 5^2?
hard.why: Odd factors ignore the power of 2: multiply the geometric sums of the 3-part and 5-part.

hard.q: What is the smallest positive integer that leaves remainder 3 when divided by 7 and remainder 5 when divided by 11?
hard.why: List numbers of the form a·k + r1 and test them against the second condition; the answers repeat every LCM.

easy.q: A price rises by 20% and then falls by 20%. What is the net percentage change (a negative value means a fall)?
easy.why: Multiply the factors: (1+u)(1-d) and compare with 1. Successive changes are not added.

easy.q: A shopkeeper buys an item for ₹1250 and sells it for ₹1500. What is his profit percentage?
easy.why: Profit % is always on cost price: (SP-CP)/CP × 100.

easy.q: After an increase of 15%, a number becomes 1380. What was the original number?
easy.why: New = original × (1+p/100), so divide; do not subtract p% of the new value.

easy.q: A price rises by 25% and then falls by 10%. What is the net percentage change (a negative value means a fall)?
easy.why: Multiply the factors: (1+u)(1-d) and compare with 1. Successive changes are not added.

easy.q: A shopkeeper buys an item for ₹800 and sells it for ₹680. What is his profit percentage?
easy.why: Profit % is always on cost price: (SP-CP)/CP × 100.

easy.q: After an increase of 8%, a number becomes 2160. What was the original number?
easy.why: New = original × (1+p/100), so divide; do not subtract p% of the new value.

medium.q: A jacket has a marked price of ₹2500. Two successive discounts of 20% and 10% are given. What is the selling price in ₹?
medium.why: Apply the discounts one after the other: MP × (1-d1) × (1-d2).

medium.q: A trader marks his goods 40% above cost price and then allows a discount of 25%. What is his profit or loss percentage (negative means loss)?
medium.why: SP = CP × 7/5 × 3/4; compare with CP.

medium.q: Anita's salary is 25% more than Beena's. Beena's salary is what percentage less than Anita's?
medium.why: Take Beena = 100, Anita = 100+p; the gap is measured against Anita.

medium.q: A shopkeeper wants 20% profit on an article costing ₹600 after giving a 10% discount. At what price in ₹ should it be marked?
medium.why: SP = CP(1+g); MP = SP/(1-d).

medium.q: Anita's salary is 60% more than Beena's. Beena's salary is what percentage less than Anita's?
medium.why: Take Beena = 100, Anita = 100+p; the gap is measured against Anita.

medium.q: A trader marks his goods 30% above cost price and then allows a discount of 10%. What is his profit or loss percentage (negative means loss)?
medium.why: SP = CP × 13/10 × 9/10; compare with CP.

hard.q: A dealer uses a weight of 900 g in place of 1 kg. He marks his goods 20% above cost and gives a 10% discount. What is his overall profit percentage?
hard.why: Combine the two effects as multiplication: (1000/w) × (1+m)(1-d) - 1.

hard.q: A man sells two articles at the same price. He gains 20% on one and loses 20% on the other. What is his overall gain or loss percentage (negative means loss)?
hard.why: Assume each sells for ₹100 and find the two cost prices; compare total cost with 200.

hard.q: The price of sugar rises by 25%. A family cuts its consumption so that spending rises by only 10%. By what percentage did consumption fall?
hard.why: Expenditure = price × quantity, so quantity factor = (1+s)/(1+r).

hard.q: A student needs 40% to pass. He scores 280 marks and fails by 50 marks. What is the maximum mark of the paper?
hard.why: Passing marks = got + shortfall = pp% of the maximum.

hard.q: By what percentage must a trader mark up his cost so that after successive discounts of 10% and 20% he still earns a profit of 26%?
hard.why: Set CP = 100; SP = 100+g; divide by both discount factors.

hard.q: A man sells two articles at the same price. He gains 30% on one and loses 30% on the other. What is his overall gain or loss percentage (negative means loss)?
hard.why: Assume each sells for ₹100 and find the two cost prices; compare total cost with 200.

easy.q: ₹6000 is divided among three friends in the ratio 2:3:5. How much does the second friend get (in ₹)?
easy.why: Share = total × (own part)/(sum of parts).

easy.q: A sum of ₹1800 is split between A and B so that A gets 2/3 of what B gets. How much does B get (in ₹)?
easy.why: A:B = a:b, so B's share is total × b/(a+b).

easy.q: The ratio of boys to girls in a club is 3:5. After 12 more girls join, the ratio becomes 1:2. How many members were there originally?
easy.why: Let the numbers be ak and bk; write the new ratio equation and solve for k.

easy.q: Rice at ₹60/kg is mixed with rice at ₹80/kg to get a mixture worth ₹68/kg. In what ratio (cheaper : dearer) are they mixed?
easy.why: Alligation: cheaper : dearer = (dearer - mean) : (mean - cheaper).

easy.q: A:B = 2:3 and B:C = 4:5. Which of these is A:B:C?
easy.why: Make B the same in both ratios (use LCM of the B terms).

easy.q: ₹9000 is divided among three friends in the ratio 1:2:6. How much does the second friend get (in ₹)?
easy.why: Share = total × (own part)/(sum of parts).

medium.q: Rice at ₹120/kg is mixed with rice at ₹150/kg to get a mixture worth ₹138/kg. In what ratio (cheaper : dearer) are they mixed?
medium.why: Alligation: cheaper : dearer = (dearer - mean) : (mean - cheaper).

medium.q: A vessel holds 100 litres of pure milk. 20 litres are removed and replaced with water. This is done once more. How many litres of milk remain?
medium.why: Each replacement multiplies the milk by (1 - x/L).

medium.q: The ratio of boys to girls in a club is 4:7. After 10 more girls join, the ratio becomes 1:2. How many members were there originally?
medium.why: Let the numbers be ak and bk; write the new ratio equation and solve for k.

medium.q: Rice at ₹40/kg is mixed with rice at ₹65/kg to get a mixture worth ₹55/kg. In what ratio (cheaper : dearer) are they mixed?
medium.why: Alligation: cheaper : dearer = (dearer - mean) : (mean - cheaper).

medium.q: A vessel holds 80 litres of pure milk. 20 litres are removed and replaced with water. This is done once more. How many litres of milk remain?
medium.why: Each replacement multiplies the milk by (1 - x/L).

medium.q: A:B = 2:3, B:C = 4:5 and C:D = 6:7. What is A:D?
medium.why: Chain the ratios by making the common terms equal, or multiply the fractions A/B × B/C × C/D.

hard.q: Vessel P has milk and water in the ratio 3:2; vessel Q has them in the ratio 1:4. In what ratio (P:Q) should the two be mixed to get milk and water in the ratio 1:1?
hard.why: Convert each to milk fraction and apply alligation on those fractions, not on the raw ratios.

hard.q: A 60-litre mixture has milk and water in the ratio 2:1. How many litres must be drawn out and replaced by water so that the ratio becomes 1:1?
hard.why: Milk left must be half the total: milk × (1 - x/L) = L/2.

hard.q: The incomes of Ravi and Sunil are in the ratio 5:4 and their expenditures in the ratio 3:2. Each saves ₹800. What is Ravi's income in ₹?
hard.why: Write income = ak, expense = cm; use savings equality to get two equations and solve.

hard.q: A 90-litre mixture has milk and water in the ratio 5:4. How many litres must be drawn out and replaced by water so that the ratio becomes 1:1?
hard.why: Milk left must be half the total: milk × (1 - x/L) = L/2.

hard.q: Vessel P has milk and water in the ratio 7:3; vessel Q has them in the ratio 1:4. In what ratio (P:Q) should the two be mixed to get milk and water in the ratio 1:1?
hard.why: Convert each to milk fraction and apply alligation on those fractions, not on the raw ratios.

hard.q: The incomes of Ravi and Sunil are in the ratio 9:7 and their expenditures in the ratio 4:3. Each saves ₹2000. What is Ravi's income in ₹?
hard.why: Write income = ak, expense = cm; use savings equality to get two equations and solve.

easy.q: A car covers the first half of a journey at 40 km/h and the second half at 60 km/h. What is its average speed in km/h?
easy.why: Equal distances: average speed is the harmonic mean 2ab/(a+b), not the simple average.

easy.q: A 150 m long train runs at 54 km/h. How many seconds does it take to cross a pole?
easy.why: Convert km/h to m/s by multiplying by 5/18; then time = length/speed.

easy.q: A runner moves at 72 km/h. What is his speed in m/s?
easy.why: Multiply km/h by 5/18 to get m/s.

easy.q: Two towns are 180 km apart. Two cyclists start from them at the same time towards each other at 25 km/h and 35 km/h. After how many hours do they meet?
easy.why: Moving towards each other, speeds add: time = distance/(a+b).

easy.q: A car covers the first half of a journey at 30 km/h and the second half at 60 km/h. What is its average speed in km/h?
easy.why: Equal distances: average speed is the harmonic mean 2ab/(a+b), not the simple average.

easy.q: A 240 m long train runs at 72 km/h. How many seconds does it take to cross a pole?
easy.why: Convert km/h to m/s by multiplying by 5/18; then time = length/speed.

medium.q: A boat goes 24 km downstream in 3 hours and returns upstream in 4 hours. What is the speed of the stream in km/h?
medium.why: Stream = (downstream speed - upstream speed)/2.

medium.q: Two trains of lengths 150 m and 170 m run in opposite directions at 66 km/h and 54 km/h. How many seconds do they take to cross each other completely?
medium.why: Relative speed adds for opposite directions; distance is the sum of the lengths.

medium.q: Walking at 3/4 of his usual speed, a man reaches office 20 minutes late. What is his usual time (in minutes)?
medium.why: Time is inversely proportional to speed: extra time = T(q/p - 1) = t.

medium.q: A cyclist rides three equal stretches at 30, 40 and 60 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole trip in km/h?
medium.why: Average speed = total distance / total time = 3 / (1/a+1/b+1/c).

medium.q: Walking at 5/6 of his usual speed, a man reaches office 15 minutes late. What is his usual time (in minutes)?
medium.why: Time is inversely proportional to speed: extra time = T(q/p - 1) = t.

medium.q: A boat goes 36 km downstream in 3 hours and returns upstream in 6 hours. What is the speed of the stream in km/h?
medium.why: Stream = (downstream speed - upstream speed)/2.

hard.q: Two trains start at the same time from stations A and B towards each other. After meeting, the one from A takes 9 hours to reach B and the one from B takes 4 hours to reach A. What is the ratio of their speeds (A's : B's)?
hard.why: After meeting, speed ratio = √(t2/t1) because each covers the other's pre-meeting distance.

hard.q: In a 100 m race A beats B by 10 m and B beats C by 20 m. By how many metres does A beat C in a 100 m race?
hard.why: When A finishes, B has run (100-x); B's run of 100 corresponds to C's (100-y), so scale.

hard.q: Walking at 4 km/h a man reaches his office 10 minutes late; at 5 km/h he reaches 5 minutes early. How far is his office (in km)?
hard.why: Distance/s1 - Distance/s2 = (late + early) in hours.

hard.q: Two runners start together from one point of a 400 m circular track and run in opposite directions at 5 m/s and 3 m/s. How many times do they meet in the first 290 seconds (not counting the start)?
hard.why: Opposite directions: they meet every C/(a+b) seconds; count whole meetings.

hard.q: Two trains start at the same time from stations A and B towards each other. After meeting, the one from A takes 16 hours to reach B and the one from B takes 25 hours to reach A. What is the ratio of their speeds (A's : B's)?
hard.why: After meeting, speed ratio = √(t2/t1) because each covers the other's pre-meeting distance.

hard.q: Walking at 3 km/h a man reaches his office 15 minutes late; at 4 km/h he reaches 5 minutes early. How far is his office (in km)?
hard.why: Distance/s1 - Distance/s2 = (late + early) in hours.

easy.q: A can finish a job in 12 days and B in 24 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
easy.why: Add the daily rates: 1/a + 1/b, then take the reciprocal.

easy.q: A can finish a job in 10 days and B in 15 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
easy.why: Add the daily rates: 1/a + 1/b, then take the reciprocal.

easy.q: A can complete a task in 30 days. He works for 12 days and then leaves. How many more days would he need to finish it?
easy.why: Work left = 1 - d/a; at 1/a per day, days left = a - d.

easy.q: A tap fills a tank in 8 hours and an outlet empties the full tank in 24 hours. If both are opened together, in how many hours is the empty tank filled?
easy.why: Net rate = 1/a - 1/b (the outlet works against the tap).

easy.q: A can finish a job in 20 days and B in 30 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
easy.why: Add the daily rates: 1/a + 1/b, then take the reciprocal.

easy.q: A can complete a task in 24 days. He works for 9 days and then leaves. How many more days would he need to finish it?
easy.why: Work left = 1 - d/a; at 1/a per day, days left = a - d.

medium.q: A and B together can do a job in 12 days, B and C in 15 days, and C and A in 20 days. In how many days can all three together do it?
medium.why: Add the three pair rates to get twice the combined rate of A, B, C.

medium.q: A alone can do a job in 20 days and B alone in 30 days. They work together for 6 days, then A leaves. How many more days does B need to finish?
medium.why: Subtract the work done together from 1 and divide by B's daily rate.

medium.q: A, B and C can do a job alone in 6, 8 and 12 days respectively. They finish it together and are paid ₹2700, shared in proportion to work done. What does B get (in ₹)?
medium.why: Share is proportional to efficiency (1/days), not to days taken.

medium.q: A tap fills a tank in 6 hours and an outlet empties the full tank in 15 hours. If both are opened together, in how many hours is the empty tank filled?
medium.why: Net rate = 1/a - 1/b (the outlet works against the tap).

medium.q: A and B together can do a job in 10 days, B and C in 15 days, and C and A in 12 days. In how many days can all three together do it?
medium.why: Add the three pair rates to get twice the combined rate of A, B, C.

medium.q: A, B and C can do a job alone in 10, 15 and 30 days respectively. They finish it together and are paid ₹3900, shared in proportion to work done. What does B get (in ₹)?
medium.why: Share is proportional to efficiency (1/days), not to days taken.

hard.q: A can do a job in 10 days and B in 15 days. They work on alternate days, A working on day 1. In how many days is the job finished?
hard.why: Work out one two-day cycle, count full cycles, then handle the last partial day.

hard.q: Pipe A fills a tank in 6 hours, pipe B in 12 hours, and a leak empties the full tank in 36 hours. With all three working, how many hours to fill the empty tank?
hard.why: Net rate = fill rates - leak rate; the answer is the reciprocal.

hard.q: 100 men are engaged to finish a job in 40 days. After 20 days only 1/4 of the job is done. How many extra men are needed to finish on time, at the same pace per man?
hard.why: Find work per man per day from what is done, then the men needed for the rest in the remaining days.

hard.q: A and B together can do a job in 12 days, B and C in 15 days, and C and A in 20 days. In how many days can A alone do it?
hard.why: Total rate of A, B and C minus (B+C) rate gives A's rate.

hard.q: 60 men are engaged to finish a job in 45 days. After 15 days only 1/5 of the job is done. How many extra men are needed to finish on time, at the same pace per man?
hard.why: Find work per man per day from what is done, then the men needed for the rest in the remaining days.

hard.q: A can do a job in 8 days and B in 12 days. They work on alternate days, A working on day 1. In how many days is the job finished?
hard.why: Work out one two-day cycle, count full cycles, then handle the last partial day.

easy.q: What is the simple interest on ₹12000 at 6% per annum for 3 years?
What is the amount on ₹10000 at 10% per annum compound interest (compounded yearly) after 2 years?
easy.why: Amount = P(1+r/100)^t.

easy.q: At simple interest a sum doubles in 8 years. What is the annual rate of interest?
easy.why: Interest = principal, so P = P·r·n/100 and r = 100/n.

easy.q: A sum earns simple interest of ₹960 in 3 years at 8% per annum. What is the sum (in ₹)?
What is the amount on ₹5000 at 20% per annum compound interest (compounded yearly) after 2 years?
easy.why: Amount = P(1+r/100)^t.

easy.q: What is the simple interest on ₹8000 at 7% per annum for 4 years?

medium.q: What is the difference between compound interest and simple interest on ₹8000 at 5% per annum for 2 years?
medium.why: For 2 years CI - SI = P(r/100)^2.

medium.q: At simple interest a sum becomes 3 times itself in 10 years. In how many years will it become 5 times itself?
medium.why: Rate per year = (k1-1)/n of principal; years = (k2-1)/that.

medium.q: What is the amount on ₹10000 for 1 year at 10% per annum compounded half-yearly?
medium.why: Half-yearly: rate r/2 per period and 2 periods.

medium.q: ₹4000 is lent at 8% simple interest for 3 years and another sum at 6% for 2 years, earning equal interest. What is the second sum (in ₹)?
medium.why: Set P1·r1·t1 = P2·r2·t2.

medium.q: What is the difference between compound interest and simple interest on ₹25000 at 8% per annum for 2 years?
medium.why: For 2 years CI - SI = P(r/100)^2.

medium.q: At simple interest a sum becomes 2 times itself in 5 years. In how many years will it become 4 times itself?
medium.why: Rate per year = (k1-1)/n of principal; years = (k2-1)/that.

hard.q: A loan of ₹21000 at 10% compound interest per year is repaid in two equal yearly instalments. What is each instalment (in ₹)?
hard.why: Present value of the instalments equals the loan: x/(1+r) + x/(1+r)^2 = P.

hard.q: A sum becomes ₹6050 in 2 years and ₹6655 in 3 years at compound interest (compounded yearly). What is the sum (in ₹)?
hard.why: The one-year growth factor is A3/A2; undo it twice from A2.

hard.q: A loan of ₹26400 at 20% compound interest per year is repaid in two equal yearly instalments. What is each instalment (in ₹)?
hard.why: Each instalment x must satisfy x/1.2 + x/1.44 = 26400, so x = 26400 × 1.44 / 2.2 = ₹17,280.

hard.q: What is the difference between compound interest and simple interest on ₹10000 at 10% per annum for 3 years?
At compound interest a sum doubles in 5 years. In how many years will it become 8 times itself?
hard.why: 8 = 2^3, so three doubling periods are needed.

hard.q: For 2 years the simple interest on a sum is ₹2000 and the compound interest exceeds it by ₹50. What is the annual rate?
hard.why: CI - SI (2 yrs) = one-year SI × r, so r = difference ÷ one-year SI.

easy.q: What is the average of 12, 15, 18, 23, 27?
easy.why: Average = sum ÷ number of values.

easy.q: The average of 9 numbers is 20. A new number 30 is included. What is the new average?
easy.why: New sum = old sum + new number; divide by the new count.

easy.q: The average of three numbers is 30. Two of them are 24 and 41. What is the third?
easy.why: Third = total - sum of the other two.

easy.q: A class of 30 students has an average mark of 60 and another class of 20 students has an average of 70. What is the combined average?
easy.why: Weight each average by the number of students.

easy.q: What is the average of 7, 9, 16, 22?
easy.why: Average = sum ÷ number of values.

easy.q: The average of 11 numbers is 42. A new number 6 is included. What is the new average?
easy.why: New sum = old sum + new number; divide by the new count.

medium.q: The average weight of 8 people goes up by 2.5 kg when a new person replaces one weighing 65 kg. What is the weight of the new person (in kg)?
medium.why: Total increase = n × rise in average; add it to the replaced weight.

medium.q: A class of 40 students has an average mark of 55 and another class of 60 students has an average of 70. What is the combined average?
medium.why: Weight each average by the number of students.

medium.q: A batter's average after 9 matches is 42. How many runs must he score in the next match to raise his average to 45?
medium.why: Required runs = new total - old total.

medium.q: The average weight of 12 people goes up by 3 kg when a new person replaces one weighing 48 kg. What is the weight of the new person (in kg)?
medium.why: Total increase = n × rise in average; add it to the replaced weight.

medium.q: The average age of 6 people in a room is 28 years. When one person leaves, the average of the rest becomes 26 years. How old was the person who left?
medium.why: Old total - new total = the age of the person who left.

medium.q: A class of 25 students has an average mark of 64 and another class of 15 students has an average of 48. What is the combined average?
medium.why: Weight each average by the number of students.

hard.q: A batsman scores 120 runs in his 12th innings and this raises his average by 3 runs. What is his average after the 12th innings?
hard.why: New average A satisfies nA = (n-1)(A-d) + x, giving A = x - (n-1)d.

hard.q: The average of 11 numbers is 50. The average of the first 6 of them is 49 and the average of the last 6 is 52. What is the 6th number?
hard.why: The two groups overlap only in the middle number: (sum of both groups) - total = that number.

hard.q: The average of 9 numbers is 40. The average of the first 5 of them is 38 and the average of the last 5 is 43. What is the 5th number?
hard.why: The two groups overlap only in the middle number: (sum of both groups) - total = that number.

hard.q: A batsman scores 85 runs in his 20th innings and this raises his average by 2 runs. What is his average after the 20th innings?
hard.why: New average A satisfies nA = (n-1)(A-d) + x, giving A = x - (n-1)d.

hard.q: The average of 13 numbers is 30. The average of the first 7 of them is 28 and the average of the last 7 is 33. What is the 7th number?
hard.why: The two groups overlap only in the middle number: (sum of both groups) - total = that number.

hard.q: A batter's average after 24 matches is 36. How many runs must he score in the next match to raise his average to 38?
hard.why: Required runs = new total - old total.

easy.q: Solve for x: 5x + 7 = 2x + 22.
easy.why: Collect x terms on one side and constants on the other.

easy.q: If the roots of x² - 9x + 20 = 0 are α and β, what is α + β?
easy.why: Sum of roots = -(coefficient of x)/(coefficient of x²).

easy.q: What are the roots of x² - 13x + 36 = 0?
easy.why: Find two numbers with sum equal to the coefficient and product equal to the constant.

easy.q: For what value of k does kx² + 12x + 9 = 0 have two equal roots?
easy.why: Equal roots need discriminant b² - 4ac = 0.

easy.q: Solve for x: 7x + 3 = 4x + 24.
easy.why: Collect x terms on one side and constants on the other.

easy.q: If the roots of x² - 11x + 24 = 0 are α and β, what is α + β?
easy.why: Sum of roots = -(coefficient of x)/(coefficient of x²).

medium.q: If 3x + 2y = 16 and 5x + 2y = 20, what is x + y?
medium.why: Eliminate one variable, solve, then add.

medium.q: The sum of two positive numbers is 17 and their product is 60. What is the larger number?
medium.why: They are the roots of x² - sx + p = 0.

medium.q: A rectangular plot has a perimeter of 28 m and an area of 48 m². What is the length of its longer side (in m)?
medium.why: Sides are the roots of x² - (half perimeter)x + area = 0.

medium.q: For what value of k does kx² + 10x + 5 = 0 have two equal roots?
medium.why: Equal roots need discriminant b² - 4ac = 0.

medium.q: If 2x + 3y = 22 and 4x + 5y = 40, what is x + y?
medium.why: Eliminate one variable, solve, then add.

medium.q: The sum of two positive numbers is 19 and their product is 84. What is the larger number?
medium.why: They are the roots of x² - sx + p = 0.

hard.q: If α and β are the roots of x² - 7x + 10 = 0, what is α² + β²?
hard.why: α² + β² = (α+β)² - 2αβ.

hard.q: If α and β are the roots of x² - 6x + 5 = 0, what is α³ + β³?
hard.why: α³ + β³ = (α+β)³ - 3αβ(α+β).

hard.q: The roots of a quadratic x² - 10x + c = 0 differ by 4. What is c?
hard.why: (α-β)² = (α+β)² - 4αβ, so αβ = ((α+β)² - d²)/4.

hard.q: For how many integer values of k between -20 and 20 (inclusive) does x² + kx + 16 = 0 have real roots?
hard.why: Real roots need k² - 4a ≥ 0; count integers k outside (-2√a, 2√a).

hard.q: How many pairs of positive integers (x, y) satisfy 5x + 7y = 187?
hard.why: Find one solution, then the others differ by steps of b in x and a in y.

hard.q: If α and β are the roots of x² - 5x + 4 = 0, what is α³ + β³?
hard.why: α³ + β³ = (α+β)³ - 3αβ(α+β).

easy.q: How many integers x satisfy |x - 5| < 3?
easy.why: This means -b < x - a < b; count integers strictly inside.

easy.q: What is the largest integer x for which 3x - 4 < 20?
easy.why: Solve 3x < 24, x < 8; strict inequality, so take the largest integer below.

easy.q: How many integers x satisfy (x - 2)(x - 9) < 0?
easy.why: The product is negative between the roots; the roots themselves are excluded.

easy.q: What is the minimum value of |x - 3| + |x - 11|?
easy.why: The sum of distances from x to two points is least when x lies between them, and equals the gap.

easy.q: How many integers x satisfy |x + 2| < 6?
easy.why: This means -b < x - a < b; count integers strictly inside.

easy.q: What is the largest integer x for which 4x - 6 < 30?
easy.why: Solve 4x < 36, x < 9; strict inequality, so take the largest integer below.

medium.q: How many integers x satisfy (x + 3)(x - 5) ≤ 0?
medium.why: The product is non-positive from -l to r, with both endpoints included.

medium.q: What is the minimum value of |x - 2| + |x - 9| + |x - 14|?
medium.why: For three points the sum is least at the middle point; it equals the distance between the outer two.

medium.q: What is the minimum value of 2x² - 8x + 15 over all real x?
medium.why: Minimum of ax²+bx+c is c - b²/(4a) when a > 0.

medium.q: If x + y = 18 with x, y positive reals, what is the maximum value of xy?
medium.why: The product is largest when x = y = s/2.

medium.q: How many integers x satisfy (x + 4)(x - 7) < 0?
medium.why: The product is negative between the roots; the roots themselves are excluded.

medium.q: What is the largest real value of x that satisfies |x - 2| + |x - 10| = 12?
medium.why: Outside the interval between a and b the sum is 2x-(a+b) or (a+b)-2x; set it equal to c.

hard.q: How many integer pairs (x, y) satisfy |x| + |y| ≤ 6?
hard.why: For each x, y runs over 2(n-|x|)+1 values; add them up (the count is 2n²+2n+1).

hard.q: How many integer pairs (x, y) satisfy |x| + |y| = 9?
hard.why: For each nonzero x there are two y values; the points form a diamond with 4a points.

hard.q: For positive x, what is the minimum value of x + 16/x?
hard.why: AM-GM: x + k/x ≥ 2√k, with equality at x = √k.

hard.q: For positive x, what is the minimum value of x + 7/x?
hard.why: AM-GM: x + k/x ≥ 2√k, with equality at x = √k.

hard.q: What is the largest real value of x that satisfies |x - 1| + |x - 7| = 10?
hard.why: Outside the interval between a and b the sum is 2x-(a+b) or (a+b)-2x; set it equal to c.

hard.q: How many integer pairs (x, y) satisfy |x| + |y| ≤ 10?
hard.why: For each x, y runs over 2(n-|x|)+1 values; add them up (the count is 2n²+2n+1).

easy.q: If f(x) = 2x² - 3x + 5, what is f(4)?
easy.why: Substitute x and follow the order of operations (square first).

easy.q: If f(x) = 2x + 3 and g(x) = 4x - 1, what is f(g(2))?
easy.why: Work from the inside: first g(x), then apply f to that result.

easy.q: What is the value of ⌊3.5⌋ + ⌊-3.5⌋, where ⌊t⌋ is the greatest integer not exceeding t?
easy.why: For a non-integer x, ⌊x⌋ + ⌊-x⌋ = -1.

easy.q: If f(x) = 3x² - 2x + 1, what is f(-2)?
easy.why: Substitute x and follow the order of operations (square first).

easy.q: If f(x) = 3x - 2 and g(x) = x + 5, what is f(g(3))?
easy.why: Work from the inside: first g(x), then apply f to that result.

easy.q: A function satisfies f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y) for all positive integers and f(1) = 4. What is f(6)?
easy.why: Repeated addition gives f(n) = n·f(1).

medium.q: A linear function f satisfies f(1) = 7 and f(2) = 10. What is f(5)?
medium.why: Slope = f(2) - f(1); extend from f(2) by three more steps.

medium.q: If f(x) = 2x + 1, what is f(f(f(3)))?
medium.why: Apply f three times in sequence.

medium.q: A function satisfies f(x) + 2f(1/x) = 6x for all x ≠ 0. What is f(2)?
medium.why: Write the equation for x and for 1/x, then eliminate f(1/x).

medium.q: What is the value of ⌊1/5⌋ + ⌊2/5⌋ + ... + ⌊12/5⌋ where ⌊t⌋ is the greatest integer not exceeding t?
medium.why: Group the terms: each value m appears k times (until the last block).

medium.q: Let f(x) = x + 5 for x < 0, f(x) = 2x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 4 and f(x) = 12 - x for x > 4. What is f(f(-3))?
medium.why: Evaluate the inner f first and pick the correct piece for the result.

medium.q: A function satisfies f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y) for all positive integers and f(1) = 3. What is f(9)?
medium.why: Repeated addition gives f(n) = n·f(1).

hard.q: A function satisfies f(x) + 2f(1/x) = 9x for all x ≠ 0. What is f(3)?
hard.why: Write the equation for x and for 1/x, then eliminate f(1/x).

hard.q: What is the maximum value of the function min(2x + 1, 10 - x) over all real x?
hard.why: The minimum of an increasing and a decreasing line peaks where they cross.

hard.q: A function has f(1) = 3 and f(n + 1) = f(n) + n for every positive integer n. What is f(8)?
What is the value of ⌊1/6⌋ + ⌊2/6⌋ + ... + ⌊20/6⌋ where ⌊t⌋ is the greatest integer not exceeding t?
hard.why: Group the terms: each value m appears k times (until the last block).

hard.q: For f(x) = x² - 3x + 5, how many real values of x satisfy f(x) = x?
hard.why: f(x) = x gives x² - (a+1)x + b = 0; check the discriminant.

hard.q: Let f(x) = x + 5 for x < 0, f(x) = 2x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 4 and f(x) = 12 - x for x > 4. What is f(f(2))?
hard.why: Evaluate the inner f first and pick the correct piece for the result.

easy.q: What is the value of log base 3 of 81?
easy.why: log_b(b^n) = n.

easy.q: What is the value of log base 2 of 1/32?
easy.why: 1/b^n = b^(-n), so the log is -n.

easy.q: If log base 5 of x = 3, what is x?
easy.why: Convert to exponential form: x = b^value.

easy.q: What is the value of log₁₀ 4 + log₁₀ 25?
easy.why: log a + log b = log(ab).

easy.q: What is the value of log base 7 of 49?
easy.why: log_b(b^n) = n.

easy.q: If log₁₀ 2 = a, what is log₁₀ 5 in terms of a?
easy.why: 5 = 10/2, so log 5 = log 10 - log 2.

medium.q: What is the value of (log base 2 of 8) × (log base 8 of 32)?
medium.why: Change of base: log_a b × log_b c = log_a c.

medium.q: Find x if log base 2 of (x + 3) + log base 2 of (x - 3) = 4.
medium.why: Combine into log_b(x²-c²) = d, solve, and reject any x that makes a log argument negative.

medium.q: Given log₁₀ 2 = 0.3010, how many digits does 2^30 have?
medium.why: Digits = floor(n·log₁₀ 2) + 1.

medium.q: What is the value of log₂ 2 + log₂ 4 + log₂ 8 + ... + log₂ 256?
medium.why: The terms are 1, 2, ..., n; add them.

medium.q: If log base 2 of p = 5 and log base 3 of q = 3, what is p + q?
medium.why: Convert each to exponential form, then add.

medium.q: What is the value of (log base 3 of 9) × (log base 9 of 81)?
medium.why: Change of base: log_a b × log_b c = log_a c.

hard.q: If log base 2 of (log base 3 of (log base 4 of x)) = 0, what is x?
hard.why: Work outward: log_a(...) = 0 means the inside is 1; repeat.

hard.q: What is the value of (log₂ 3)(log₃ 4)(log₄ 5)(log₅ 6)(log₆ 7)(log₇ 8)?
hard.why: The product telescopes to log₂ 8 = 3.

hard.q: If x satisfies (log₂ x)² - 4·log₂ x + 3 = 0, what is the product of the two possible values of x?
hard.why: The roots in log₂ x are 1 and c, so the x values are 2 and 2^c; product = 2^(c+1).

hard.q: Given log₁₀ 2 = 0.3010, how many digits does 2^100 have?
hard.why: Digits = floor(n·log₁₀ 2) + 1.

hard.q: Find x if log base 5 of (x + 12) + log base 5 of (x - 12) = 2.
hard.why: Combine into log_b(x²-c²) = d, solve, and reject any x that makes a log argument negative.

hard.q: If log base 5 of (log base 2 of (log base 3 of x)) = 0, what is x?
hard.why: Work outward: log_a(...) = 0 means the inside is 1; repeat.

easy.q: The first term of an AP is 5 and the common difference is 4. What is its 12th term?
easy.why: nth term = a + (n-1)d.

easy.q: What is the sum of the first 15 terms of the AP 3, 7, 11, ...?
The first term of a GP is 3 and the common ratio is 2. What is the 7th term?
easy.why: nth term = a·r^(n-1).

easy.q: What is the sum to infinity of the GP 18, 6, 2, ...?
easy.why: S∞ = a/(1-r) when |r| < 1.

easy.q: How many terms are there in the AP 7, 12, 17, ..., 112?
easy.why: n = (last - first)/d + 1.

easy.q: The first term of a GP is 2 and the common ratio is 3. What is the 5th term?
easy.why: nth term = a·r^(n-1).

medium.q: In an AP the 3rd term is 17 and the 7th term is 37. What is the 20th term?
medium.why: Find d from the two terms, then a, then the nth term.

medium.q: What is the sum of all positive integers below 100 that are multiples of 3 or 5 (or both)?
medium.why: Add the two AP sums and subtract the multiples of the LCM that were counted twice.
Each term is 1/k - 1/(k+1), so the sum telescopes to 1 - 1/(n+1).

medium.q: What is the sum of the first 6 terms of the GP 2, 6, 18, ...?
What is the geometric mean of 4 and 36?
medium.why: GM = √(ab).

medium.q: In an AP the 3rd term is 11 and the 7th term is 27. What is the 15th term?
medium.why: Find d from the two terms, then a, then the nth term.

hard.q: What is the value of 1×2 + 2×3 + 3×4 + ... + 10×11?
What is the sum of all positive integers below 200 that are multiples of 4 or 6 (or both)?
hard.why: Add the two AP sums and subtract the multiples of the LCM that were counted twice.

hard.q: Three numbers in AP have sum 27 and product 693. What is the largest of them?
hard.why: Let them be a-d, a, a+d; the sum gives a, the product gives d.

hard.q: The sum of the first n terms of the GP 5, 10, 20, ... is 635. What is n?
hard.why: Use S = a(r^n - 1)/(r - 1) and solve for the power of r.

hard.q: What is the value of 1² + 2² + 3² + ... + 20²?
What is the sum of all positive integers below 500 that are multiples of 7 or 11 (or both)?
hard.why: Add the two AP sums and subtract the multiples of the LCM that were counted twice.

easy.q: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2:3:4. What is the largest angle in degrees?
easy.why: Angles sum to 180°; divide in the ratio.

easy.q: The two shorter sides of a right-angled triangle are 9 cm and 12 cm. What is the hypotenuse in cm?
easy.why: Pythagoras: c² = a² + b².

easy.q: A chord of a circle of radius 13 cm is 5 cm from the centre. What is the length of the chord in cm?
easy.why: Half-chord = √(r² - d²); the chord is twice that.

easy.q: In a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, angle A = 105°. What is angle C?
easy.why: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°.

easy.q: The two shorter sides of a right-angled triangle are 20 cm and 21 cm. What is the hypotenuse in cm?
easy.why: Pythagoras: c² = a² + b².

easy.q: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 3:4:5. What is the largest angle in degrees?
easy.why: Angles sum to 180°; divide in the ratio.

medium.q: What is the inradius of a right triangle with legs 6 cm and 8 cm?
medium.why: For a right triangle r = (a + b - c)/2, or area divided by semi-perimeter.

medium.q: In triangle ABC, AB = 12 cm, AC = 18 cm and BC = 15 cm. The bisector of angle A meets BC at D. What is BD in cm?
medium.why: Angle bisector theorem: BD/DC = AB/AC.

medium.q: A point is 13 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 5 cm. What is the length of the tangent from the point to the circle in cm?
medium.why: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius: t² = d² - r².

medium.q: Two chords AB and CD of a circle meet at P inside it. PA = 6, PB = 8 and PC = 4. What is PD?
medium.why: Intersecting chords: PA·PB = PC·PD.

medium.q: From an external point P, a secant meets a circle at A and B (A nearer P) with PA = 4 and AB = 5. What is the length of the tangent from P?
medium.why: Tangent-secant theorem: PT² = PA·PB.

medium.q: What is the inradius of a right triangle with legs 8 cm and 15 cm?
medium.why: For a right triangle r = (a + b - c)/2, or area divided by semi-perimeter.

hard.q: What is the inradius of a triangle with sides 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm?
hard.why: r = Area/s, with the area from Heron's formula.

hard.q: Two circles of radii 8 cm and 3 cm have centres 13 cm apart. What is the length of their direct (external) common tangent in cm?
hard.why: Direct common tangent: √(d² - (r1 - r2)²).

hard.q: Two circles of radii 5 cm and 3 cm lie apart with centres 17 cm apart. What is the length of their transverse (internal) common tangent in cm?
hard.why: Transverse common tangent: √(d² - (r1 + r2)²).

hard.q: What is the circumradius of a triangle with sides 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm?
hard.why: R = abc/(4 × Area); find the area by Heron's formula.

hard.q: A triangle has sides 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm. What is the altitude on the side of 14 cm?
hard.why: Area from Heron's formula, then altitude = 2 × Area / base.

hard.q: What is the inradius of a triangle with sides 17 cm, 25 cm and 26 cm?
hard.why: r = Area/s, with the area from Heron's formula.

easy.q: What is the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm, in cm³? (Use π = 22/7.)
easy.why: V = πr²h.

easy.q: What is the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 12 cm and 18 cm and distance 10 cm between them, in cm²?
easy.why: A = ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × height.

easy.q: What is the volume of a cone of base radius 7 cm and height 6 cm, in cm³? (Use π = 22/7.)
easy.why: V = (1/3)πr²h.

easy.q: The volume of a cube is 512 cm³. What is its total surface area in cm²?
easy.why: Edge = ∛V; total surface area = 6 × edge².

easy.q: What is the volume of a sphere of radius 21 cm, in cm³? (Use π = 22/7.)
What is the volume of a cylinder of radius 14 cm and height 5 cm, in cm³? (Use π = 22/7.)
easy.why: V = πr²h.

medium.q: A solid metal sphere of radius 9 cm is melted and recast into small spheres of radius 3 cm. How many small spheres are formed?
medium.why: Volumes are equal, so the count is (R/r)³.

medium.q: A sphere of radius 3 cm is dropped fully into a cylindrical jar of radius 6 cm that has enough water to cover it. By how many cm does the water level rise?
medium.why: Rise × πR² = (4/3)πr³.

medium.q: The radius of a sphere is increased by 10%. By what percentage does its volume increase?
medium.why: Volume scales as the cube of the radius: (1+p)³ - 1.

medium.q: A solid cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 12 cm is melted into a cone of the same base radius. What is the height of the cone in cm?
medium.why: Cone volume is a third of a cylinder with the same base and height, so the height triples.

medium.q: What is the curved surface area of a cone with base radius 7 cm and height 24 cm, in cm²? (Use π = 22/7.)
medium.why: Slant height l = √(r²+h²); CSA = πrl.

medium.q: What is the total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 7 cm, in cm²? (Use π = 22/7.)
medium.why: Curved part 2πr² plus flat base πr² gives 3πr².

hard.q: A cube of side 8 cm is painted on all faces and then cut into 1 cm cubes. How many of the small cubes have exactly two faces painted?
hard.why: Edge cubes (not corners): 12 edges × (n-2).

hard.q: A cube of side 7 cm is painted on all faces and then cut into 1 cm cubes. How many of the small cubes have exactly one face painted?
hard.why: Face-centre cubes: 6 faces × (n-2)².

hard.q: A sector of radius 21 cm and angle 120° is rolled into a cone. What is the curved surface area of the cone in cm²? (Use π = 22/7.)
hard.why: The cone's slant height is the sector radius and its curved area equals the sector area.

hard.q: A solid cuboid 44 cm × 21 cm × 12 cm is melted into a cylinder of radius 7 cm. What is the height of the cylinder in cm? (Use π = 22/7.)
hard.why: Equal volumes: abc = πr²h.

hard.q: A cube of side 10 cm is painted on all faces and then cut into 1 cm cubes. How many of the small cubes have no face painted?
hard.why: Inner cube: (n-2)³.

hard.q: A sphere is melted and recast into 27 equal small spheres. How many times the original surface area is the total surface area of the small spheres?
hard.why: Each small radius is R/k; total area = n·4π(R/k)² = k × 4πR².

easy.q: What is the distance between (3, 4) and (9, 12)?
easy.why: Distance = √((x2-x1)² + (y2-y1)²).

easy.q: What is the midpoint of the segment joining (2, 8) and (10, -4)?
easy.why: Midpoint = average of the x's and of the y's.

easy.q: What is the slope of the line through (1, 2) and (5, 10)?
easy.why: Slope = rise/run = (y2-y1)/(x2-x1).

easy.q: What is the distance between (-2, 3) and (4, -5)?
easy.why: Distance = √((x2-x1)² + (y2-y1)²).

easy.q: What is the midpoint of the segment joining (-6, 1) and (4, 9)?
easy.why: Midpoint = average of the x's and of the y's.

easy.q: What is the slope of the line through (2, 9) and (6, 1)?
easy.why: Slope = rise/run = (y2-y1)/(x2-x1).

medium.q: What is the area of the triangle with vertices (1, 1), (7, 1) and (4, 9)?
What are the coordinates of the point that divides the segment joining (2, 3) and (12, 8) internally in the ratio 2:3?
medium.why: Section formula: (m·x2 + n·x1)/(m+n); the ratio weights the far point.

medium.q: A line passes through (2, 5) and (6, 13). Where does it cut the y-axis?
medium.why: Find the slope, then c = y - mx.

medium.q: What is the area of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (8, 3) and (2, 7)?
What are the coordinates of the point that divides the segment joining (-3, 4) and (7, -6) internally in the ratio 3:2?
medium.why: Section formula: (m·x2 + n·x1)/(m+n); the ratio weights the far point.

medium.q: A line passes through (1, 7) and (4, 1). Where does it cut the y-axis?
medium.why: Find the slope, then c = y - mx.

hard.q: What is the perpendicular distance of the point (2, 1) from the line 3x + 4y - 25 = 0?
hard.why: Distance = |Ax1 + By1 + C|/√(A²+B²).
hard.topic: Distance from a point to a line

hard.q: What is the distance between the parallel lines 3x + 4y = 5 and 3x + 4y = 35?
hard.why: Distance = |C1 - C2|/√(A²+B²).
hard.topic: Distance from a point to a line

hard.q: A line through the point (4, 3) cuts the positive axes at A and B, with (4, 3) as the midpoint of AB. What is the area of triangle OAB (O is the origin)?
hard.why: The midpoint gives A = (2p, 0) and B = (0, 2q); area = ½(2p)(2q).

hard.q: What is the area of the quadrilateral with vertices (0, 0), (6, 0), (8, 5), (1, 4) taken in order?
hard.why: Shoelace formula: ½|Σ(xi·yi+1 - xi+1·yi)|.

hard.q: What is the circumradius of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (12, 0) and (0, 5)?
hard.why: A right-angled triangle's circumcentre is the midpoint of its hypotenuse, so R = hypotenuse/2.

hard.q: What is the perpendicular distance of the point (2, 3) from the line 5x + 12y - 20 = 0?
hard.why: Distance = |Ax1 + By1 + C|/√(A²+B²).
hard.topic: Distance from a point to a line

easy.q: In how many ways can a committee of 3 be chosen from 8 people?
easy.why: Order does not matter: nCr.

easy.q: In how many ways can 3 different prizes be given to 7 students, if no student gets more than one?
easy.why: Order matters: nPr = n!/(n-r)!.

easy.q: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is 7?
easy.why: Count favourable pairs out of 36 equally likely outcomes.

easy.q: How many different arrangements of the letters of the word BANANA are there?
easy.why: n! divided by the factorial of each repeated letter's count.

easy.q: In how many ways can a committee of 4 be chosen from 10 people?
easy.why: Order does not matter: nCr.

easy.q: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is 9?
easy.why: Count favourable pairs out of 36 equally likely outcomes.

medium.q: 6 friends sit in a row. Two particular friends must always sit next to each other. In how many ways can they be seated?
medium.why: Treat the pair as one unit: (n-1)! arrangements × 2 orders inside.

medium.q: A fair coin is tossed 4 times. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
How many different arrangements of the letters of the word MISSISSIPPI are there?
medium.why: n! divided by the factorial of each repeated letter's count.

medium.q: A committee of 4 is to be formed from 5 men and 4 women with at least one woman. In how many ways can this be done?
medium.why: Total ways minus the ways with no woman.

medium.q: Two cards are drawn without replacement from a standard pack of 52. What is the probability that both are aces?
In how many ways can 7 people sit around a circular table?
medium.why: Fix one person; arrange the rest: (n-1)!.

hard.q: 5 letters are placed at random into 5 addressed envelopes, one each. In how many ways can every letter go into a wrong envelope?
hard.why: Count derangements by inclusion-exclusion: n!(1 - 1/1! + 1/2! - ...).

hard.q: How many non-negative integer solutions does x + y + z = 12 have?
hard.why: Stars and bars: C(n+2, 2).

hard.q: There are 10 points in a plane, of which 4 lie on one straight line and no other three are collinear. How many triangles can be formed?
hard.why: Subtract the collinear triples from all triples.

hard.q: In how many ways can the letters of the word DAUGHTER be arranged so that no two vowels are next to each other?
hard.why: Place consonants first, then put the vowels in the gaps between them.

hard.q: Two fair dice are rolled and at least one shows a 5. What is the probability that the sum is 8?
hard.why: Conditional probability: restrict to the 11 outcomes with a 5.

hard.q: If all arrangements of the letters of the word DELHI are listed in dictionary order, what is the rank of DELHI itself?
hard.why: Count words starting with each smaller letter, then continue position by position.

easy.q: In a class, 40 students play cricket, 35 play football and 15 play both. How many play at least one of the two games?
easy.why: n(A∪B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A∩B).

easy.q: Of 100 students, 60 like tea, 45 like coffee and 25 like both. How many like neither?
easy.why: Subtract the union from the total.

easy.q: In a group, 55 people speak Hindi, 38 speak Tamil and 20 speak both. How many speak only Hindi?
easy.why: Only A = n(A) - n(A∩B).

easy.q: In a class, 72 students play cricket, 50 play football and 18 play both. How many play at least one of the two games?
easy.why: n(A∪B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A∩B).

easy.q: Of 120 students, 70 like tea, 65 like coffee and 40 like both. How many like neither?
easy.why: Subtract the union from the total.

easy.q: In a group, 90 people speak Hindi, 64 speak Tamil and 30 speak both. How many speak only Hindi?
easy.why: Only A = n(A) - n(A∩B).

medium.q: In a survey, 120 people read paper A, 100 read B and 90 read C. 50 read both A and B, 40 read both B and C, 30 read both C and A, and 20 read all three. How many read at least one paper?
medium.why: Inclusion-exclusion: add singles, subtract pairs, add back the triple.

medium.q: 80 people like pizza, 70 like burgers and 60 like pasta. 30 like both pizza and burgers, 25 like both burgers and pasta, 20 like both pasta and pizza, and 10 like all three. How many like exactly two of the three?
medium.why: Each pair count includes the all-three group, so subtract it 3 times in total.

medium.q: Of 200 families, 120 own a car, 110 own a bike and 60 own both. How many own exactly one of the two?
medium.why: Exactly one = n(A) + n(B) - 2n(A∩B).

medium.q: 80 people like pizza, 70 like burgers and 60 like pasta. 30 like pizza and burgers, 25 like burgers and pasta, 20 like pasta and pizza, and 10 like all three. How many like exactly one of the three?
medium.why: Only-one = singles - 2(pair sums) + 3(triple).

medium.q: In a survey, 65 people read paper A, 70 read B and 55 read C. 25 read both A and B, 30 read both B and C, 20 read both C and A, and 10 read all three. How many read at least one paper?
medium.why: Inclusion-exclusion: add singles, subtract pairs, add back the triple.

medium.q: Of 150 families, 90 own a car, 80 own a bike and 45 own both. How many own exactly one of the two?
medium.why: Exactly one = n(A) + n(B) - 2n(A∩B).

hard.q: In a town, 70% of people read English papers, 80% read Hindi and 60% read Marathi. What is the minimum percentage that must read all three?
hard.why: Minimum overlap of all three = a + b + c - 2 × 100, if positive.

hard.q: Of 120 students, 85 play chess and 70 play carrom. What is the minimum number who play both?
hard.why: Overlap is least when the union is as large as possible, i.e. N.

hard.q: In a survey of 200 people, each likes at least one of tea, coffee and juice. 120 like tea, 110 like coffee and 100 like juice. Exactly 50 people like exactly two drinks. How many like all three?
hard.why: a+b+c = n1 + 2n2 + 3n3 and N = n1 + n2 + n3; subtract to get n2 + 2n3.

hard.q: 65 students play chess and 48 play carrom. What is the maximum possible number who play both?
hard.why: The overlap cannot exceed the smaller set.

hard.q: In a town, 85% of people read English papers, 75% read Hindi and 90% read Marathi. What is the minimum percentage that must read all three?
hard.why: Minimum overlap of all three = a + b + c - 2 × 100, if positive.

hard.q: In a survey of 150 people, each likes at least one of tea, coffee and juice. 90 like tea, 85 like coffee and 80 like juice. Exactly 35 people like exactly two drinks. How many like all three?
hard.why: a+b+c = n1 + 2n2 + 3n3 and N = n1 + n2 + n3; subtract to get n2 + 2n3.

easy.q: Which word is a collective noun?
easy.why: A herd is a group of animals taken as one.

easy.q: What is the plural of 'child'?
easy.why: Child has an irregular plural.

easy.q: In 'Her honesty impressed the teacher', which word is an abstract noun?
easy.why: Honesty is a quality you cannot touch.

easy.q: Meera is my best friend. ___ lives near my house. Choose the pronoun.
easy.why: Meera is one girl, so we use 'She'.

easy.q: What is the plural of 'knife'?
easy.why: Nouns ending in -fe change to -ves.

easy.q: Replace the noun in 'The boys played cricket' with a pronoun.
easy.why: 'The boys' is plural and third person, so 'They'.

medium.q: Which sentence has a collective noun?
o: A swarm of bees settled on the tree.
medium.why: Swarm names a group of bees.

medium.q: Which pair is correctly matched as singular and plural?
medium.why: Mouse and goose are irregular; wolf makes wolves; sheep stays sheep.

medium.q: Which is the abstract noun in 'The villagers admired Anil's courage during the flood'?
medium.why: Courage is a quality; the others are things or people.

medium.q: Ravi and I went to the market. ___ bought mangoes. Choose the pronoun.
medium.why: 'Ravi and I' is the subject, so we use 'We'.

medium.q: What are the plurals of 'baby' and 'monkey'?
medium.why: Consonant + y becomes -ies; vowel + y just adds -s.

medium.q: The teacher gave the prize to Neha and ___. Choose the correct word.
medium.why: After 'to' we need the object form 'me'.

hard.q: In 'Kabir showed kindness to the dog', the nouns Kabir, kindness and dog are respectively:
hard.why: Kabir names a person, kindness is a quality, dog is a general name.

hard.q: Which sentence has all the plurals correct?
o: The two mans carried three boxes of tomatoes.
The two men carried three boxs of tomatoes.
The two men carried three boxes of tomatoes.
The two mens carried three boxes of tomatos.
hard.why: Man becomes men; box takes -es; tomato takes -es.

hard.q: Which noun is used only in the plural form?
hard.why: Scissors is always plural in form.

hard.q: The little boy hurt ___ while climbing the wall. Choose the pronoun.
hard.why: A reflexive pronoun must match the boy: himself.

hard.q: Which noun has the same form in singular and plural?
hard.why: Deer is both one deer and many deer.

hard.q: Which sentence uses the possessive pronoun correctly?
o: This pen is my, not your.
This pen is mine, not yours.
This pen is me, not you.
This pen is mine, not your.
hard.why: Mine and yours stand alone without a noun after them.

easy.q: Choose the article: ___ apple a day keeps the doctor away.
easy.why: Apple starts with a vowel sound, so 'an'.

easy.q: Fill in: I have ___ pencils in my box. (a small number, countable)
easy.why: Few is used with countable plural nouns.

easy.q: Choose the article: She bought ___ umbrella.
easy.why: Umbrella begins with a vowel sound /u/ as in 'up'.

easy.q: Choose the demonstrative: ___ book here on my desk is new.
easy.why: 'Here' and one book mean 'This'.

easy.q: Fill in: There is ___ milk in the glass. (not full)
easy.why: Some fits an uncountable noun like milk.

easy.q: Choose the word: Aman lost ___ bag yesterday.
easy.why: 'His' is the possessive that goes before a noun.

medium.q: Choose the article: He is ___ honest boy.
medium.why: Honest starts with a vowel sound because h is silent.

medium.q: Which sentence is correct?
medium.why: Water is uncountable, so 'a little'.

medium.q: Choose the article: Ravi is ___ European student.
medium.why: European begins with a 'y' sound, a consonant sound.

medium.q: Fill in: ___ birds over there are sparrows.
medium.why: Far and plural means 'Those'.

medium.q: Which sentence is correct?
medium.why: Mangoes are countable, so 'many'.

medium.q: Fill in: The girls forgot ___ lunch boxes.
medium.why: 'Their' shows the girls own the boxes.

hard.q: Which sentence needs 'the' in the blank? ___ Ganga is a holy river.
hard.why: Names of rivers take 'the'.

hard.q: Which sentence uses 'little' correctly to mean 'almost none'?
o: There is little hope of rain today.
There is a little hope of rain today.
There are little hopes of rain.
There is few hope of rain today.
hard.why: 'Little' without 'a' is negative: hardly any.

hard.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: The sun rises in a east.
The sun rises in the east.
hard.why: Unique things like the sun take 'the', and 'the east' too.

hard.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Two those red balls are mine.
Red two those balls are mine.
Those two red balls are mine.
Those red two ball are mine.
hard.why: Determiners such as 'those' come before numbers and adjectives.

hard.q: Which sentence uses 'few' to mean 'some, enough'?
o: Few guests arrived early, so we had help.
A few guests arrived early, so we started.
hard.why: 'A few' is positive: some.

hard.q: Which sentence has the article error?
hard.why: University starts with a 'yoo' sound so 'a' is needed.

easy.q: Choose the correct verb: She ___ to school every day.
easy.why: Third person singular takes -es in simple present.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: Birds ___ in the sky now.
easy.why: Plural subject and 'now' need 'are flying'.

easy.q: Choose the past form: Yesterday, we ___ to the park.
easy.why: Go has an irregular past: went.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: Tomorrow I ___ my grandmother.
easy.why: Tomorrow shows future, so 'will visit'.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: He ___ his homework right now.
easy.why: 'Right now' needs present continuous with 'is'.

easy.q: Which sentence is in the future tense?
easy.why: 'Will play' marks the future.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: My father ___ tea every morning.
medium.why: Habit in the present; he takes -s.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: The children ___ when the teacher came in.
medium.why: Past continuous with plural subject: were talking.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: She ___ her room yesterday.
medium.why: Yesterday needs simple past.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: Next week, Priya ___ to Jaipur.
medium.why: 'Next week' shows the future.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: I ___ a letter when the lights went out.
medium.why: An action in progress in the past uses 'was writing'.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: Do you know if it ___ tomorrow?
medium.why: A future event needs 'will rain'.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: He did not go to school yesterday.
He did not went to school yesterday.
He not went to school yesterday.
He did not goes to school yesterday.
hard.why: After 'did not' use the base verb: go.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: I was read while my sister cooked.
I read while my sister was cook.
I was reading while my sister was cooking.
I am reading while my sister was cooking.
hard.why: Two actions going on together in the past use past continuous.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
hard.why: After 'does' use the base verb: play.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: The sun rises in the east.
The sun rose in the east every day.
The sun is rise in the east.
The sun rising in the east.
hard.why: General truths use the simple present.

hard.q: Which sentence has the verb tense error?
o: Yesterday I went to the market.
Tomorrow I will go to the market.
Now I am going to the market.
Yesterday I will go to the market.
hard.why: 'Yesterday' cannot be used with 'will go'.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: If it will rain tomorrow, we will stay home.
If it rains tomorrow, we will stay home.
If it rained tomorrow, we stay home.
If it rains tomorrow, we stayed home.
hard.why: After 'if' we use present, not 'will', for a future condition.

easy.q: Choose the preposition: The cat is sleeping ___ the table.
easy.why: Under shows place; the others are not prepositions of place.

easy.q: Choose the correct word: Mohan was born ___ 2014.
easy.why: Use 'in' with years.

easy.q: Choose the preposition: School starts ___ 8 o'clock.
easy.why: Use 'at' with a clock time.

easy.q: Choose the conjunction: I like tea ___ coffee.
easy.why: 'And' joins two similar things.

easy.q: Choose the correct word: We play cricket ___ Sundays.
easy.why: Use 'on' with days.

easy.q: Choose the conjunction: She was tired, ___ she kept walking.
easy.why: 'But' shows contrast.

medium.q: Choose the correct word: The bird flew ___ the window.
medium.why: Through shows movement from one side to the other.

medium.q: Choose the correct word: I am afraid ___ dogs.
medium.why: 'Afraid of' is the right phrase.

medium.q: Choose the correct word: She is good ___ painting.
medium.why: 'Good at' is the fixed phrase.

medium.q: Choose the conjunction: Hurry up, ___ you will miss the bus.
medium.why: 'Or' warns of what happens otherwise.

medium.q: Choose the correct word: He is interested ___ music.
medium.why: 'Interested in' is correct.

medium.q: Choose the conjunction: He stayed home ___ he was ill.
medium.why: 'Because' gives the reason.

hard.q: Choose the correct word: The books were divided ___ the three girls.
hard.why: Use 'among' for more than two.

hard.q: Choose the correct word: He has lived here ___ 2019.
hard.why: 'Since' goes with a starting point in time.

hard.q: Choose the correct word: The ball rolled ___ the two chairs.
hard.why: Between is used for two.

hard.q: Choose the conjunction: ___ it was raining, we went out to play.
hard.why: Although shows the surprising contrast.

hard.q: Choose the correct word: She has been waiting ___ two hours.
hard.why: 'For' goes with a length of time.

hard.q: Choose the conjunction: You cannot enter ___ you show your ticket.
hard.why: 'Unless' means 'if not'.

easy.q: Which word is an adjective in 'The red kite flew high'?
easy.why: Red describes the kite.

easy.q: Choose the adverb: She sings sweetly.
easy.why: Sweetly tells how she sings.

easy.q: Choose the comparative: Ria is ___ than Sia. (tall)
easy.why: Add -er to short adjectives to compare two.

easy.q: Choose the superlative: Mount Everest is the ___ mountain. (high)
easy.why: The superlative of high is highest.

easy.q: Choose the correct word: He runs ___. (quick)
easy.why: A verb is described by an adverb.

easy.q: Choose the correct word: This box is ___ than that one. (heavy)
easy.why: Change y to i and add -er.

medium.q: Choose the correct word: Of all the boys, Dev is the ___. (good)
medium.why: Good - better - best is irregular.

medium.q: Which word is an adverb of time? 'We will leave soon.'
medium.why: Soon tells when.

medium.q: Choose the correct word: This story is ___ than that one. (interesting)
medium.why: Long adjectives take 'more'.

medium.q: Choose the correct word: She answered the question ___. (correct)
medium.why: An adverb describes how she answered.

medium.q: Which word is an adverb of place? 'The children played outside.'
medium.why: Outside tells where.

medium.q: Choose the correct word: She is the ___ girl in the class. (young)
medium.why: Three or more things need superlative.

hard.q: Choose the correct word: He is ___ than his brother. (clever)
hard.why: Two persons: comparative; clever takes -er.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: He did good in the test.
He did goodly in the test.
He did well in the test.
He did best in the test, than me.
hard.why: 'Well' is the adverb; 'good' is an adjective.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: She is the beautifulest girl here.
She is the most beautiful girl here.
She is more beautiful girl here.
hard.why: Long adjectives take most for the superlative.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: This is the less expensive of the two bags.
This is the least expensive of the two bags.
This is the less expensive from the two bags.
hard.why: With two, we use the comparative: less.

hard.q: Which sentence has an adverb modifying an adjective?
hard.why: 'Very' describes the adjective 'hot'.

hard.q: Choose the correct sentence.
hard.why: 'Late' is the adverb meaning not on time; 'lately' means recently.

easy.q: In 'my sister lives in jaipur.' which word needs a capital letter?
easy.why: Names of places are proper nouns and begin with a capital.

easy.q: Which sentence is an exclamatory sentence?
easy.why: It shows sudden strong feeling.

easy.q: Which sentence needs a question mark?
easy.why: It is a question.

easy.q: Choose the correct sentence.
easy.why: Apostrophe replaces the o in 'do not'.

easy.q: Which is a command?
easy.why: A command tells someone to do something.

easy.q: Which sentence has a comma used correctly?
o: I bought, apples bananas and grapes.
I bought apples bananas, and, grapes.
I, bought apples bananas and grapes.
I bought apples, bananas and grapes.
easy.why: Commas separate items in a list.

medium.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
medium.why: Comma comes after the opening 'Yes'.

medium.q: Where does the comma go? 'After lunch we played cricket'.
medium.why: A comma follows an opening phrase.

medium.q: Choose the correct apostrophe: This is ___ pen.
medium.why: The apostrophe + s shows possession.

medium.q: Which is an interrogative sentence?
medium.why: It asks a question.

medium.q: Which sentence needs an exclamation mark?
medium.why: It shows excitement.

medium.q: Which sentence is declarative?
o: Is the Taj Mahal in Agra?
The Taj Mahal is in Agra.
How grand the Taj Mahal is!
medium.why: It states a fact.

hard.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
o: Mother said, please wash your hands.
Mother said: Please, wash your hands.
hard.why: Direct speech needs a comma, quotation marks and a capital letter inside.

hard.q: Many boys left bags on the bench. Which sentence is correct?
o: The boys' bags are on the bench.
The boy's bags are on the bench.
The boys bags' are on the bench.
The boys's bags are on the bench.
hard.why: Plural boys takes only an apostrophe after the s.

hard.q: Which uses 'its' and 'it's' correctly?
o: Its raining, and the dog is in it's kennel.
It's raining, and the dog is in it's kennel.
Its raining, and the dog is in its' kennel.
It's raining, and the dog is in its kennel.
hard.why: It's = it is; its = belonging to it.

hard.q: Which is the correct imperative sentence?
o: Will you pass the salt please.
hard.why: It gives a polite command.

hard.q: Which sentence has the commas right?
o: Ria my cousin, is a doctor.
Ria, my cousin, is a doctor.
Ria, my cousin is, a doctor.
Ria my, cousin is a doctor.
hard.why: Commas set off extra information.

hard.q: Which sentence is exclamatory and correctly punctuated?
hard.why: An exclamation ends with !, and 'How tall ... is' keeps the statement order.

easy.q: Choose the synonym of 'big'.
easy.why: Large means big.

easy.q: Choose the antonym of 'hot'.
easy.why: Cold is the opposite of hot.

easy.q: Choose the synonym of 'happy'.
easy.why: Glad is close in meaning to happy.

easy.q: Choose the correct word: I can ___ the bell. (hear/here)
easy.why: Hear is what ears do.

easy.q: Choose the antonym of 'early'.
easy.why: Late is the opposite of early.

easy.q: Choose the correct word: Come ___ and sit. (hear/here)
easy.why: 'Here' means in this place.

medium.q: Choose the synonym of 'begin'.
medium.why: Start means begin.

medium.q: Choose the antonym of 'ancient'.
medium.why: Modern is the opposite of ancient.

medium.q: Choose the synonym of 'brave'.
medium.why: Courageous means brave.

medium.q: Choose the right word: The ___ of the cake was delicious. (piece/peace)
medium.why: Piece means a part; peace is calm.

medium.q: Choose the antonym of 'generous'.
medium.why: Stingy means unwilling to give.

medium.q: Choose the right word: I like to ___ a book every week. (read/red)
medium.why: Read is the verb; red is a colour.

hard.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'rapid'.
hard.why: Swift means fast.

hard.q: Choose the antonym of 'victory'.
hard.why: Defeat is the opposite of victory.

hard.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'enormous'.
hard.why: Gigantic means very large.

hard.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: The principal gave a speech about good principles.
The principle gave a speech about good principals.
The principal gave a speech about good principals.
The principle gave a speech about good principles.
hard.why: Principal = head; principle = rule.

hard.q: Choose the antonym of 'expand'.
hard.why: Shrink is the opposite of expand.

hard.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Please except this gift from us.
Please accept this gift from us.
Please expect this gift from us.
Please excepting this gift from us.
hard.why: Accept means to receive; except means 'other than'.
