easy.q: Which word is a common noun in 'Priya read a book in Pune'?
easy.why: Book is a general name of a thing.

easy.q: What is the plural of 'bus'?
easy.why: Nouns ending in -s add -es.

easy.q: Which noun is a collective noun?
easy.why: A fleet is a group of ships.

easy.q: Choose the pronoun: The tree is old. ___ gives good shade.
easy.why: A tree is a thing, so 'It'.

easy.q: What is the feminine of 'actor'?
easy.why: Actor becomes actress.

easy.q: Choose the pronoun: Ali and Sam are friends. ___ study together.
easy.why: Two boys in the third person: They.

medium.q: Identify the material noun.
medium.why: Gold is the material; the others are things or people made from it.

medium.q: What is the plural of 'wife'?
medium.why: Nouns ending in -fe change to -ves.

medium.q: In 'Her patience won everyone's trust', the abstract nouns are:
medium.why: Patience and trust are ideas, not things.

medium.q: Choose the right pronoun: The book is on the shelf; please give ___ to me.
medium.why: The book is a single thing.

medium.q: Which pair has the correct masculine-feminine match?
medium.why: Nephew is male, niece is female.

medium.q: Choose the right pronoun: Neha and ___ are going to the fair.
medium.why: 'Neha and I' is the subject of 'are going'.

hard.q: Which sentence has a countable noun used correctly?
o: There are three loaves of bread on the table.
There are three breads on the table.
There is three bread on the table.
hard.why: Bread is uncountable; we count loaves.

hard.q: What is the plural of 'mother-in-law'?
hard.why: The main noun, mother, takes the plural.

hard.q: Which sentence uses a collective noun with the correct verb?
o: The class are writing a test and is tired.
The class is writing a test.
The class were writing a test and was tired.
The class have writing a test.
hard.why: When the group acts as one unit, we use a singular verb.

hard.q: Which sentence uses the reflexive pronoun correctly?
o: She taught her to swim, by herself, to herself.
She taught her self to swim.
hard.why: Herself refers back to the subject.

hard.q: Which noun has a different plural form from the others?
hard.why: Sheep keeps the same form; the others add -s.

hard.q: Which sentence has the correct relative pronoun?
o: The girl which won the race is my cousin.
The girl who won the race is my cousin.
The girl whom won the race is my cousin.
The girl whose won the race is my cousin.
hard.why: Use 'who' for a person acting as the subject.

easy.q: Choose the article: She wants to become ___ engineer.
easy.why: Engineer begins with a vowel sound.

easy.q: Choose the word: There are ___ mangoes in the basket. (a large number)
easy.why: Many is used with countable plurals.

easy.q: Choose the article: ___ moon was bright last night.
easy.why: There is only one moon, so 'the'.

easy.q: Choose the word: ___ are my shoes. (pointing to shoes near you)
easy.why: Near and plural: these.

easy.q: Choose the word: I don't have ___ money. (not enough)
easy.why: Much is used with uncountable nouns.

easy.q: Choose the word: Is ___ your bag over there?
easy.why: Far and singular: that.

medium.q: Choose the article: He is ___ one-eyed man.
medium.why: One begins with a 'w' sound, a consonant sound.

medium.q: Choose the word: Sheela has ___ friends, so she feels lonely. (hardly any)
medium.why: Few without 'a' shows a negative idea.

medium.q: Choose the article: We saw ___ hour-long film.
medium.why: Hour begins with a silent h, so a vowel sound.

medium.q: Choose the word: ___ of the two shirts fits me. (not one)
medium.why: Neither means not one of two.

medium.q: Choose the word: We have ___ time left, so let's hurry. (hardly any)
medium.why: Little shows hardly any.

medium.q: Choose the word: Each of the boys has ___ own book.
medium.why: Each is singular; 'his' matches.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: Himalayas are in the north of India.
The Himalayas is in a north of India.
The Himalayas are in the north of India.
A Himalayas are in north of India.
hard.why: Mountain ranges take 'the', and 'the north' is a direction.

hard.q: Which sentence uses a determiner correctly?
o: Every student has submitted the form.
Every students have submitted the form.
Every student have submitted the form.
All student has submitted the form.
hard.why: Every is followed by a singular noun and verb.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: She plays guitar and tabla in the evening the.
She plays the guitar and tabla the.
She plays the guitars and tabla's.
She plays the guitar and the tabla.
hard.why: Musical instruments take 'the' when we speak of playing them.

hard.q: Choose the sentence with the correct quantifier.
o: There isn't many traffic on this road.
There aren't much traffics on this road.
There isn't much traffic on this road.
There isn't few traffic on this road.
hard.why: Traffic is uncountable, so 'much'.

hard.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Both the brother is a doctor.
hard.why: Both goes with plural.

hard.q: Choose the sentence that has no article error.
o: He wants to be pilot like one in film.
He wants to be an pilot like the one in the film.
He wants to be the pilot like an one in the film.
He wants to be a pilot like the one in the film.
hard.why: A job takes 'a' (pilot starts with a consonant), 'the one' is specific.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: The sun ___ in the east.
easy.why: A fact in simple present with singular subject.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: She ___ her lunch already.
easy.why: 'Already' and singular subject: has eaten.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: They ___ football now.
easy.why: 'Now' + plural subject: are playing.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: Last year we ___ Agra.
easy.why: Last year points to simple past.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: I ___ this film twice.
easy.why: Present perfect with I: have seen.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: By tomorrow he ___ the work.
easy.why: Tomorrow shows future.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: The train ___ before we reached the station.
medium.why: Past perfect shows the earlier past action.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: She ___ for two hours when I called.
medium.why: Past perfect continuous for a longer earlier action.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: He ___ in Mumbai since 2018.
medium.why: 'Since' goes with present perfect.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: We ___ lunch when the guests arrived.
medium.why: Past continuous interrupted by another past action.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: Look! The baby ___ .
medium.why: 'Look!' signals an action now.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: My brother ___ cricket every Sunday.
medium.why: Habit: simple present.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: I have known him for ten years.
I know him for ten years.
I am knowing him for ten years.
I knew him for ten years now.
hard.why: Know is a state verb; use present perfect with 'for'.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: If I was you, I will apologise.
If I am you, I would apologise.
If I were you, I would apologise.
If I were you, I will apologise.
hard.why: An imaginary condition uses 'were' and 'would'.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: When she reached the hall, the show has begun.
When she reached the hall, the show had begun.
When she had reached the hall, the show begins.
When she reaches the hall, the show had begun.
hard.why: The show began first, so past perfect.

hard.q: Which sentence has a tense error?
o: He is going to school yesterday.
He will go to school tomorrow.
hard.why: 'Yesterday' needs a past tense.

hard.q: Which sentence has the right tense?
o: She said that she is tired yesterday.
She says that she was tiredly.
She said that she will tired.
She said that she was tired.
hard.why: Past tense said, so the next verb moves to the past.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: By the time we arrive, the match would started.
By the time we arrive, the match will have started.
By the time we will arrive, the match started.
By the time we arrive, the match had start.
hard.why: Future perfect for an action completed before a future time.

easy.q: Choose the verb: The dog ___ loudly.
easy.why: Singular subject takes -s verb.

easy.q: Choose the verb: My friend ___ a cycle.
easy.why: Singular subject: has.

easy.q: Choose the verb: The girls ___ singing.
easy.why: Plural subject: are.

easy.q: Choose the verb: Rice ___ grown in many parts of India.
easy.why: Rice is uncountable: is.

easy.q: Choose the verb: The students ___ in the hall.
easy.why: Plural subject takes are.

easy.q: Choose the verb: Ravi and Mohan ___ my cousins.
easy.why: Two persons joined by and: plural.

medium.q: Choose the verb: Neither of the boys ___ present.
medium.why: Neither is singular.

medium.q: Choose the verb: The news ___ shocking.
medium.why: News is singular in form and meaning.

medium.q: Choose the verb: Each of the players ___ a medal.
medium.why: Each is singular.

medium.q: Choose the verb: Bread and butter ___ my breakfast.
medium.why: Bread and butter is treated as one dish.

medium.q: Choose the verb: Mathematics ___ my favourite subject.
medium.why: Names of subjects ending in -ics are singular.

medium.q: Choose the verb: One of my friends ___ a doctor.
medium.why: The subject is 'one', which is singular.

hard.q: Choose the verb: The teacher along with her students ___ going on a trip.
hard.why: The subject is 'teacher'; 'along with' does not add a subject.

hard.q: Choose the verb: A number of students ___ absent today.
hard.why: A number of means many: plural.

hard.q: Choose the verb: Either Rita or her sisters ___ coming.
hard.why: The verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'sisters'.

hard.q: Choose the verb: Two hundred rupees ___ a large sum for a child.
hard.why: An amount of money as a whole is singular.

hard.q: Choose the verb: The number of absentees ___ small.
hard.why: The number is singular.

hard.q: Choose the verb: The police ___ searching for the thief.
hard.why: Police is always plural.

easy.q: Choose the word: The meeting is ___ 5 p.m.
easy.why: Use 'at' with exact time.

easy.q: Choose the word: The bird sat ___ the branch.
easy.why: Sitting on a surface: on.

easy.q: Choose the word: She was born ___ May.
easy.why: Use 'in' with months.

easy.q: Choose the word: Rani is tired ___ she worked all day.
easy.why: 'Because' gives the reason.

easy.q: Choose the word: He is fond ___ ice cream.
easy.why: 'Fond of' is the fixed phrase.

easy.q: Choose the word: Work hard, ___ you will fail.
easy.why: 'Or' warns about the other result.

medium.q: Choose the word: The ship sailed ___ the river.
medium.why: Down the river shows direction.

medium.q: Choose the word: The shop is ___ the bank and the post office.
medium.why: Between for two things.

medium.q: Choose the word: He jumped ___ the wall.
medium.why: Over crosses the top of the wall.

medium.q: Choose the word: I like tea, ___ my sister prefers coffee.
medium.why: 'But' shows contrast.

medium.q: Choose the word: She is married ___ a doctor.
medium.why: 'Married to' is correct.

medium.q: Choose the word: He worked hard ___ he passed.
medium.why: 'So' shows the result.

hard.q: Choose the word: He died ___ cancer.
hard.why: We say 'died of' an illness.

hard.q: Choose the word: I'll go ___ it rains heavily.
hard.why: 'Unless' means 'if not'.

hard.q: Choose the word: The fine was imposed ___ him for speeding.
hard.why: Fine is imposed on a person.

hard.q: Choose the word: She is senior ___ me.
hard.why: 'Senior to' (not than).

hard.q: Choose the word: ___ she was ill, she attended the class.
hard.why: 'Though' shows contrast.

hard.q: Choose the word: The book was written ___ a famous author.
hard.why: By marks the doer of an action.

easy.q: Choose the comparative: Sara is ___ than Maya. (short)
easy.why: Comparing two: add -er.

easy.q: Which word is an adjective? 'The tall boy ran home.'
easy.why: Tall describes the boy.

easy.q: Choose the superlative: He is the ___ boy in class. (smart)
easy.why: Comparing many: -est.

easy.q: Choose the word: She speaks ___. (soft)
easy.why: An adverb modifies the verb.

easy.q: Which word is an adverb? 'He walked slowly.'
easy.why: Slowly says how he walked.

easy.q: Choose the word: This is the ___ cake I have eaten. (good)
easy.why: Irregular superlative: best.

medium.q: Choose the word: This is the ___ of the two paths. (short)
medium.why: Two things use comparative.

medium.q: Which is an adjective of quantity?
medium.why: Some tells how much.

medium.q: Choose the word: She is ___ intelligent than her brother.
medium.why: Long adjective comparatives take 'more'.

medium.q: Which is an adverb of frequency?
medium.why: Often tells how frequently.

medium.q: Which is a demonstrative adjective? 'That boy is my cousin.'
medium.why: That points to a noun.

medium.q: Choose the word: He ran ___ to catch the bus. (fast)
medium.why: Fast is both adjective and adverb.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: She is the most cleverest girl in the class.
She is the clever girl in the class.
She is the cleverest girl in the class.
hard.why: Double superlatives are wrong.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: Of the two brothers, Rahul is the elder.
Of the two brothers, Rahul is the eldest.
Of the two brothers, Rahul is oldest.
Of two, Rahul is most elder.
hard.why: Two persons: comparative 'elder'.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: He is more senior than me.
He is the senior than me.
hard.why: Senior, junior, superior take 'to'.

hard.q: Which sentence contains an adverb that modifies another adverb?
o: She is a very good singer.
hard.why: 'Very' modifies the adverb 'beautifully'.

hard.q: Which sentence uses 'hard' and 'hardly' correctly?
o: She works hardly and hard rests.
She works hard and hardly rests.
She works hardly and rests hard.
hard.why: Hard = with effort; hardly = almost not.

hard.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Hardly we had reached when it rained.
Hardly had we reach when it rains.
We hardly had reached when it rained.
Hardly had we reached when it rained.
hard.why: 'Hardly had' is followed by the past participle and 'when'.

easy.q: Choose the synonym of 'quick'.
easy.why: Fast is close to quick.

easy.q: Choose the correct word: We ___ our friends at the station. (meet/meat)
easy.why: Meet means to come together.

easy.q: Choose the antonym of 'rich'.
easy.why: Poor is opposite of rich.

easy.q: A person who writes books is called a(n)
easy.why: An author writes books.

easy.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
easy.why: I before e except after c.

easy.q: Choose the antonym of 'always'.
easy.why: Never is the opposite.

medium.q: Choose the synonym of 'ancient'.
medium.why: Ancient means very old.

medium.q: Choose the correct word: The ___ is shining brightly. (sun/son)
medium.why: Sun is the star; son is a boy.

medium.q: Choose the antonym of 'arrive'.
medium.why: Depart is opposite of arrive.

medium.q: One who treats sick people is a(n)
medium.why: A doctor treats the sick.

medium.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
medium.why: One c, two s.

medium.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom 'a piece of cake'.
medium.why: The idiom means something easy.

hard.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'reluctant'.
hard.why: Reluctant means unwilling.

hard.q: Choose the correct word: The new rule will ___ all students. (affect/effect)
hard.why: Affect is the verb meaning to influence.

hard.q: Choose the antonym of 'transparent'.
hard.why: Opaque lets no light through.

hard.q: One word for 'a person who cannot read or write'.
hard.why: Illiterate is the correct word.

hard.q: Choose the correct spelling.
hard.why: The correct spelling is conscience.

hard.q: The idiom 'to burn the midnight oil' means:
hard.why: It means to study or work late.

easy.q: What is the next number in the sequence 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, ...?
easy.why: The sequence goes up by 5 each time, so 25 + 5 = 30.

easy.q: What is the 6th square number?
easy.why: The 6th square number is 6 x 6 = 36. Doubling 6 gives 12, which is a common slip.

easy.q: What is the next number in the triangular sequence 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, ...?
easy.why: The gaps grow by 1 each time: +2, +3, +4, +5, so the next gap is +6 and 15 + 6 = 21.

easy.q: Which of these is a cube number?
easy.why: 125 = 5 x 5 x 5. The others cannot be written as a number multiplied by itself three times.

easy.q: What is the next number in 100, 93, 86, 79, ...?
easy.why: Each term is 7 less than the one before, so 79 - 7 = 72.

easy.q: What is the value of 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9?
easy.why: The sum of the first 5 odd numbers is 5 x 5 = 25.

medium.q: What is the 10th triangular number?
medium.why: Add 1 + 2 + ... + 10 = 55. 45 is the 9th triangular number.

medium.q: What is the sum of the first 12 odd numbers?
medium.why: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n x n, so 12 x 12 = 144.

medium.q: The 6th and 7th triangular numbers are 21 and 28. What do you get when you add them?
medium.why: 21 + 28 = 49 = 7 x 7. Two neighbouring triangular numbers always add to a square number.

medium.q: A staircase has 1 tile in step 1, 3 tiles in step 2, 6 in step 3 and 10 in step 4. How many tiles are in step 8?
medium.why: The tiles are triangular numbers. Step 8 has 1 + 2 + ... + 8 = 36. 28 is step 7.

medium.q: In the sequence 1, 3, 7, 15, 31, ... each term is double the previous one plus 1. What is the next term?
medium.why: 31 x 2 + 1 = 63. Adding 32 gives 63 too: each gap doubles.

medium.q: Which number is both a square number and a cube number?
medium.why: 64 = 8 x 8 and 64 = 4 x 4 x 4. 8 and 125 are cubes only; 16 is a square only.

hard.why: The sum going up to n and back down is n x n = 50 x 50 = 2500.

hard.q: Which of these numbers can be arranged as a triangle of dots and also as a square of dots?
hard.why: 36 is the 8th triangular number and 6 x 6. 28 and 45 are only triangular, 49 is only square.
The powers of 2 up to 512 add to 1023. Adding 1 gives 1024 = 2 x 512.

hard.q: The hexagonal numbers 1, 7, 19, 37, 61, 91 grow by 6, 12, 18, 24, 30. What is the next number?
hard.why: The next gap is 36, so 91 + 36 = 127.

hard.q: What do you get when you add the 20th and the 21st triangular numbers?
hard.why: Two consecutive triangular numbers add up to a square. Here 210 + 231 = 441 = 21 x 21.
Pair the terms: 40 x 41 / 2 = 820. 1640 forgets to divide by 2.

easy.q: How many straight lines can be drawn through two different points?
easy.why: Two points fix one straight line. Infinitely many lines pass through a single point.

easy.q: Which figure has one starting point and goes on forever in one direction?
easy.why: A ray starts at one point and goes on endlessly one way. A line goes both ways; a segment has two ends.

easy.q: An angle measures 120°. What type of angle is it?
easy.why: An obtuse angle is more than 90° and less than 180°.

easy.q: An angle measures 200°. What type of angle is it?
easy.why: A reflex angle is more than 180° and less than 360°.

easy.q: How many degrees does a straight angle have?
easy.why: A straight angle makes a straight line, which is 180°.

easy.q: Which of these is an acute angle?
easy.why: Acute angles are less than 90°.

medium.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 4 o'clock?
medium.why: Each hour mark is 30° apart, so 4 hours = 4 x 30° = 120°.

medium.q: An angle has one arm along the 20° mark of a protractor scale and the other along the 115° mark of the same scale. How big is the angle?
medium.why: Subtract the two readings on the same scale: 115° - 20° = 95°.

medium.q: Two angles of a triangle are 50° and 60°. What is the third angle?
medium.why: The three angles of a triangle add up to 180°, so 180° - 110° = 70°.

medium.q: A wheel has 12 equally spaced spokes. What is the angle between two neighbouring spokes?
medium.why: A full turn is 360°, and 360° / 12 = 30°.

medium.q: Two angles 65° and 40° are placed side by side. What type of angle do they make together?
medium.why: 65° + 40° = 105°, which is between 90° and 180°.

medium.q: A straight line is cut by a ray into two angles. One angle is 128°. How big is the other angle?
medium.why: The two angles make 180°, so 180° - 128° = 52°.

hard.q: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 3:30?
hard.why: At 3:30 the minute hand is at 180° and the hour hand at 3.5 x 30° = 105°. The difference is 75°.

hard.q: Six points are marked so that no three are on one straight line. How many different lines can be drawn through pairs of points?
hard.why: Each point joins 5 others: 6 x 5 = 30, but each line is counted twice, so 15.

hard.q: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. How big is the largest angle?
hard.why: 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 parts = 180°, so 1 part = 20°. The largest is 4 x 20° = 80°.

hard.q: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 10:20?
hard.why: Minute hand: 20 x 6° = 120°. Hour hand: 10 x 30° + 10° = 310°. The difference is 190°, so the smaller angle is 360° - 190° = 170°.

hard.q: Rays OB, OC and OD lie on one side of the straight line AOD. ∠AOB = 40°, and ∠BOC is 25° more than ∠AOB. What is ∠COD?
hard.why: ∠BOC = 65°. On a straight line 40° + 65° + ∠COD = 180°, so ∠COD = 75°.

hard.q: The clock shows exactly 6:00. How big is the smaller angle between the hands at 6:40?
hard.why: Minute hand at 40 x 6° = 240°. Hour hand at 180° + 20° = 200°. The difference is 40°.

easy.q: What is the digit sum of 6482?
Which number reads the same forwards and backwards?
easy.why: 4554 reversed is 4554. 4545 reversed is 5454.

easy.q: What is the largest 4-digit number you can make with the digits 3, 8, 1, 5, using each once?
easy.why: Put the biggest digits first: 8, 5, 3, 1.

easy.q: What is the smallest 3-digit number you can make with the digits 4, 0, 7, using each once?
easy.why: A number cannot start with 0, so start with 4, then the smaller digit 0, then 7.

easy.q: Estimate 4897 + 3102 by rounding each number to the nearest hundred.
Which of these clock times is a palindrome (ignoring the colon)?
easy.why: 1221 reads the same both ways. 1234, 1112 and 1020 do not.

medium.q: How many times is the digit 7 written when you write all numbers from 1 to 100?
medium.why: 7 appears 10 times as a units digit and 10 times as a tens digit (70 to 79). 77 uses it twice.

medium.q: Make the largest and the smallest number from the digits of 5264. What is largest minus smallest?
What is the smallest 3-digit number whose digits add up to 15?
medium.why: Keep the hundreds digit as small as possible: 1. Then the tens digit as small as possible: 5 with units 9.

medium.q: Start with 57. Add its reverse. If you do not get a palindrome, repeat with the new number. How many additions give a palindrome?
medium.why: 57 + 75 = 132, not a palindrome. 132 + 231 = 363, a palindrome. That is 2 additions.

medium.q: A digital clock shows 12:21, a palindrome. How many minutes later is the next palindromic time, 13:31?
medium.why: From 12:21 to 13:21 is 60 minutes, and 10 more to 13:31. Total 70 minutes.

medium.q: Using the digits 7, 2, 9, 0 once each (no number may start with 0), what is the largest number minus the smallest number?
medium.why: Largest is 9720, smallest is 2079. 9720 - 2079 = 7641.

hard.q: How many times is the digit 7 written when you write all numbers from 1 to 1000?
hard.why: Each of the units, tens and hundreds places has 7 exactly 100 times in 1 to 1000. 3 x 100 = 300.

hard.q: Take 3524. Repeat: largest rearrangement minus smallest rearrangement (4 digits). After how many steps do you reach 6174?
What is the smallest 5-digit palindrome that is greater than 23456?
hard.why: 23432 is less than 23456. The next palindrome of the form 23c32 is 23532.

hard.q: How many 4-digit palindromes have digits that add up to 14?
hard.why: A 4-digit palindrome is ABBA, so 2A + 2B = 14 and A + B = 7. A can be 1 to 7, so there are 7.

hard.q: What is the largest 5-digit number between 40,000 and 80,000 that has only odd digits, with no digit repeated?
hard.why: Start with 7 (9 would put it above 80,000). Then use the biggest odd digits left: 9, 5, 3, 1.

hard.q: Start with 78. Add its reverse, and keep repeating with each new number until you get a palindrome. How many additions are needed?

easy.q: In a tally chart one bundle of five and three single marks are drawn. What is the frequency?
easy.why: A bundle stands for 5, plus 3 more is 8.

easy.q: In a pictograph one symbol stands for 20 kites. The symbols for Tuesday are 5. How many kites were sold on Tuesday?
easy.why: 5 symbols x 20 kites = 100 kites.

easy.q: In a bar graph, the bar for Monday is taller than the bar for Tuesday. What does this tell you?
o: Both days have the same value
easy.why: A taller bar means a bigger value on the same scale.

easy.q: Which of these needs you to collect data by asking people?
o: The number of days in June
The number of letters in INDIA
The favourite ice-cream flavour of your class
easy.why: Facts that are already known do not need a survey. Favourites need asking.

easy.q: A table shows marks and number of students: 3 marks: 4 students, 4 marks: 6 students, 5 marks: 5 students. How many students are there in all?
One symbol stands for 10 apples. How many symbols are needed to show 60 apples?
easy.why: 60 / 10 = 6 symbols.

medium.q: Shoe sizes of 10 students are 5, 6, 6, 7, 5, 6, 8, 7, 6, 5. How many students wear size 6 or bigger?
medium.why: Size 6 has 4 students, size 7 has 2 and size 8 has 1. 4 + 2 + 1 = 7.

medium.q: In a pictograph one symbol stands for 40 cycles. Monday shows 3 symbols and Tuesday shows 5 symbols. How many cycles were sold on both days together?
medium.why: 3 + 5 = 8 symbols, and 8 x 40 = 320.

medium.q: A die is rolled 20 times. The faces 1 to 6 show 3, 4, 2, 5, 3, 3 times. On how many rolls did the die show 5 or 6?
medium.why: Face 5 showed 3 times and face 6 showed 3 times, so 6.

medium.q: On a bar graph, 1 unit of height stands for 5 students. A bar is 7 units tall. How many students does it show?
A table shows wickets taken and matches: 0 wickets in 4 matches, 1 wicket in 6 matches, 2 wickets in 5 matches, 3 wickets in 2 matches. How many wickets in total?
Votes for class monitor: Asha 14, Bilal 9, Chitra 17, Dev 10. By how many votes did the winner beat the runner-up?
medium.why: Chitra won with 17 and Asha was second with 14. 17 - 14 = 3.

hard.q: A table shows wickets and matches: 0 wickets in 6 matches, 1 in 9, 2 in 7, 3 in 5, 4 in 3. How many wickets in total?
In a pictograph 1 symbol stands for 6 students. Meena has 13 symbols and Kabir has 6 and a half symbols. Meena says she has more than double Kabir's number. Is she right?
o: No, because 6 and a half is more than half of 13
hard.why: Meena has 13 x 6 = 78 and Kabir has 6.5 x 6 = 39. 78 = 2 x 39 exactly, not more than double.

hard.q: 75 students chose a sport: cricket 24, football 18, hockey 15 and the rest kabaddi. On a bar graph 1 cm stands for 3 students. How tall is the kabaddi bar?
hard.why: Kabaddi = 75 - 57 = 18 students. 18 / 3 = 6 cm.

hard.q: 40 students scored marks: 5 marks: 6 students, 6 marks: 11, 7 marks: x, 8 marks: 9, 9 marks: 4. What is x?
A pictograph with 1 symbol = 30 books has rows of 4, 6, 2 and 8 symbols. The scale is changed to 1 symbol = 60 books. How many symbols are there in all now?
hard.why: Total books = 20 x 30 = 600. 600 / 60 = 10 symbols.

hard.q: A bar graph on a 1 cm = 4 students scale shows cricket 9 cm, football 7 cm and hockey 5 cm. 120 students were asked and the rest chose kabaddi. How tall is the kabaddi bar?
hard.why: Cricket 36 + football 28 + hockey 20 = 84. Kabaddi = 120 - 84 = 36 students, and 36 / 4 = 9 cm.

easy.q: Which of these is a prime number?
easy.why: 29 has only two factors, 1 and 29. 27, 33 and 39 are all multiples of 3.

easy.q: How many factors does 12 have?
easy.why: The factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12.

easy.q: What is the greatest number that divides both 8 and 12?
easy.why: Common factors of 8 and 12 are 1, 2 and 4. The greatest is 4.

easy.q: Which is the prime factorisation of 36?
easy.why: Prime factorisation uses primes only. 6, 4 and 9 are not prime.

easy.q: Which pair of numbers is co-prime?
easy.why: 8 and 15 share only the factor 1. The other pairs share 3, 6 and 7.

easy.q: Which is the only even prime number?
easy.why: 2 has only two factors, 1 and 2. Every other even number also has 2 as a factor, so it has more than two.

medium.q: How many prime numbers are there between 20 and 40?
medium.why: The primes are 23, 29, 31 and 37.

medium.q: What is the smallest number that both 12 and 18 divide into?
medium.why: 12 = 2 x 2 x 3 and 18 = 2 x 3 x 3. The smallest common multiple is 2 x 2 x 3 x 3 = 36.

medium.q: Which digit can replace * in 52* to make the number divisible by 3?
medium.why: 5 + 2 + 2 = 9, which is a multiple of 3. The other digits give 10, 11 and 13.

medium.q: I am a 2-digit odd number. I am divisible by both 5 and 7, and my digits add up to 8. Who am I?
medium.why: Multiples of 35: 35 and 70. 35 is odd and 3 + 5 = 8.

medium.q: What is the total number of prime factors in the prime factorisation of 72 (counting repeats)?
medium.why: 72 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 3, so 5 prime factors.

medium.q: What is the smallest number that has three different prime factors?
medium.why: 2 x 3 x 5 = 30. Any smaller number has at most two different prime factors.

hard.q: What is the smallest number that is divisible by every number from 1 to 8?
hard.why: Take the highest power of each prime: 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 5 x 7 = 840.

hard.q: Two bells ring every 12 minutes and 18 minutes, and a third rings every 20 minutes. They all ring together at 8:00 am. When do they next ring together?
hard.why: The smallest common multiple of 12, 18 and 20 is 180 minutes, which is 3 hours. 8:00 + 3 hours = 11:00 am.

hard.q: The number 7*58 is divisible by 11. Which digit is *?
hard.why: For 11, the sums of digits in alternate places must differ by 0 or 11. (7 + 5) = 12 and (* + 8), so * + 8 = 12 and * = 4. Check: 7458 = 11 x 678.

hard.q: How many prime numbers are there between 90 and 130?
What is the smallest multiple of 6 that has exactly 8 factors?
hard.why: 24 has factors 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24 (8 factors). 12 has 6, 36 has 9, 48 has 10.

hard.q: What is the largest 4-digit number that is divisible by 12?
hard.why: 9999 / 12 leaves 3, so subtract 3: 9996 = 12 x 833.

easy.q: A rectangle is 12 cm long and 8 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
easy.why: Perimeter = 2 x (12 + 8) = 40 cm. 96 is the area.

easy.q: A square park has sides of 9 m. What is the distance around it?
What is the area of a rectangle 15 m long and 6 m wide?
easy.why: Area = 15 x 6 = 90 sq m. 42 is the perimeter.

easy.q: What is the perimeter of an equilateral triangle with side 7 cm?
easy.why: 3 equal sides: 3 x 7 = 21 cm.

easy.q: What is the area of a square with side 11 cm?
easy.why: Area = 11 x 11 = 121 sq cm. 44 is the perimeter.

easy.q: A rectangle has area 72 sq cm and length 9 cm. What is its breadth?
easy.why: Breadth = area / length = 72 / 9 = 8 cm.

medium.q: A field is 45 m long and 30 m wide. Fencing costs ₹20 per metre. What is the cost of fencing all around?
medium.why: Perimeter = 2 x (45 + 30) = 150 m. Cost = 150 x 20 = ₹3,000. 27,000 uses the area by mistake.

medium.q: A wire is bent into a rectangle 18 cm by 12 cm. It is straightened and bent into a square. What is the side of the square?
medium.why: Wire length = 2 x (18 + 12) = 60 cm. Square side = 60 / 4 = 15 cm.

medium.q: A rectangular track is 80 m long and 50 m wide. Ravi runs 3 rounds. How far does he run?
medium.why: One round = 2 x (80 + 50) = 260 m. 3 rounds = 780 m.

medium.q: A rectangle is 10 m by 6 m. A 4 m by 3 m corner is cut out. What is the area left?
A floor is 12 m by 8 m. Tiles cost ₹50 per sq m. What is the cost of tiling the floor?
A 48 cm string forms a square. What is the side of the square?
medium.why: A square has 4 equal sides, so 48 / 4 = 12 cm.

hard.q: A rectangle has area 96 sq cm and perimeter 40 cm. What is its longer side?
hard.why: Length + breadth = 20. The pair of numbers that add to 20 and multiply to 96 is 12 and 8.

hard.q: A garden is 24 m by 18 m. A path 2 m wide runs inside along all four sides. What is the area of the path?
hard.why: Inner garden = (24 - 4) x (18 - 4) = 20 x 14 = 280. Path = 432 - 280 = 152. 168 forgets the corners.

hard.q: A rectangular park is 250 m by 150 m. Rakhi walks 2 km along its edge. How many rounds does she make?
A square park of side 40 m has a path 5 m wide all around it outside. What is the area of the path?
hard.why: Outer square side = 50 m, so area 2500. Park = 1600. 2500 - 1600 = 900. 800 forgets the 4 corner squares.

hard.q: A rectangle is 14 m by 6 m. A square has the same perimeter. Which has the larger area, and by how much?
hard.why: Perimeter 40 m so the square side is 10 m, area 100. The rectangle has 84. 100 - 84 = 16.

hard.q: An equilateral triangle of side 12 cm and a square have the same perimeter. What is the area of the square?
hard.why: Triangle perimeter = 36 cm, so the square side is 9 cm and its area is 81 sq cm.

easy.q: What is 3/8 + 2/8?
easy.why: The denominators are the same, so add the numerators: 3 + 2 = 5, giving 5/8.

easy.q: Which fraction is equal to 1/2?
Write 2 1/3 as an improper fraction.
Write 9/4 as a mixed number.
easy.why: 9 / 4 = 2 remainder 1, so 2 and 1/4.

easy.q: What is 6/8 in its simplest form?
easy.why: Divide the top and bottom by 2 to get 3/4.

easy.q: 3 rotis are shared equally among 4 children. How much does each child get?
easy.why: Each roti is cut in 4 and each child takes one part from each: 3/4.

medium.q: What is 2/3 + 1/4?
medium.why: Common denominator 12: 8/12 + 3/12 = 11/12.

medium.q: Which list shows 1/2, 2/3 and 3/8 from smallest to largest?
medium.why: In 24ths they are 12/24, 16/24 and 9/24. So the order is 9, 12, 16.

medium.q: What is 5/6 - 1/4?
medium.why: Common denominator 12: 10/12 - 3/12 = 7/12.

medium.q: Write 3 2/5 as an improper fraction.
Ravi paints 1/3 of a wall and Sia paints 1/4 of the same wall. What part of the wall is not painted?
Which fraction is equal to 3/5?
medium.why: Multiply top and bottom by 4: 3/5 = 12/20.

hard.q: A box has a missing number: box - 2/9 = 1/3. What number goes in the box?
A tank is 3/4 full. In the morning 1/6 of the tank is used and in the evening 1/3 of the tank is used. What part of the tank is left?
Which list shows 2/3, 3/4, 5/6 and 7/9 from largest to smallest?
hard.why: In 36ths they are 24, 27, 30 and 28. Largest to smallest: 30, 28, 27, 24.

hard.q: Rani reads 1/4 of a 200-page book on Monday and 2/5 of it on Tuesday. How many pages are left?
hard.why: Monday 50 pages and Tuesday 80 pages, so 130 read. 200 - 130 = 70.

hard.q: What is the smallest fraction that must be added to 5/6 to make 1 1/2?

easy.q: Which tool do you use to draw a circle of radius 4 cm?
easy.why: A compass keeps a fixed distance from a centre point, which makes a circle.

easy.q: A circle has radius 5.5 cm. What is its diameter?
easy.why: Diameter is twice the radius: 2 x 5.5 = 11 cm.

easy.q: How big is each corner angle of a rectangle?
easy.why: All four angles of a rectangle are right angles.

easy.q: The four angles of a rectangle add up to how many degrees?
easy.why: 4 right angles: 4 x 90° = 360°.

easy.q: A rectangle has sides 7 cm and 4 cm. What is the length of the side opposite the 7 cm side?
easy.why: Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal.

easy.q: Which statement is true for a square?
easy.why: A square has four equal sides and four right angles.

medium.q: In rectangle ABCD one diagonal AC is 10 cm. What is the other diagonal BD?
medium.why: The two diagonals of a rectangle are equal in length.

medium.q: A rectangle is made from three identical squares of side 4 cm placed side by side. What is its perimeter?
medium.why: The rectangle is 12 cm by 4 cm. 2 x (12 + 4) = 32 cm.

medium.q: A circle's diameter AB is 14 cm and O is the centre. How far is O from A?
medium.why: The centre is the midpoint of a diameter, so OA = 14 / 2 = 7 cm.

medium.q: In a rectangle the diagonal makes an angle of 35° with one side. What angle does it make with the adjacent side at the same corner?
medium.why: The corner is 90°, so the other part is 90° - 35° = 55°.

medium.q: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD meet at O. Diagonal AC = 14 cm. What is OA?
medium.why: The diagonals of a rectangle cut each other into equal halves, so OA = 14 / 2 = 7 cm.

medium.q: Which statement is true?
o: A rectangle has four equal sides
medium.why: A square has four right angles, so it is a special rectangle with equal sides.

hard.q: Circle A has radius 5 cm and circle B has radius 3 cm. Their centres are 8 cm apart. How many points do the two circles have in common?
hard.why: 5 + 3 = 8, so the circles just touch at one point.

hard.q: A rectangle 20 cm by 12 cm is divided into the biggest possible equal squares. How many squares are there?
hard.why: The biggest side that fits both is 4 cm. 20 / 4 = 5 squares along and 12 / 4 = 3 across: 15 squares.

hard.q: In a rectangle the diagonal splits one corner into two angles in the ratio 5 : 4. What is the bigger angle?
hard.why: 5 + 4 = 9 parts = 90°, so 1 part = 10°. The bigger angle is 50°.

hard.q: A four-sided figure has all sides equal but its angles are not 90°. What is it called?
hard.why: Equal sides with no right angles is a rhombus, not a square.

hard.q: Rectangle ABCD has diagonals that meet at O and AC = 18 cm. What is OA + OB + OC + OD?
hard.why: Each of the four halves is 18 / 2 = 9 cm, so 4 x 9 = 36 cm.

hard.q: To construct rectangle ABCD with AB = 7 cm and diagonal AC = 9 cm, you draw AB and a perpendicular at B. How do you find C with a compass?
hard.why: C is 9 cm from A and lies on the perpendicular at B, so the arc is centred at A with radius 9 cm.

easy.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
easy.why: Two through opposite corners and two through midpoints of opposite sides.

easy.q: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
easy.why: One from each corner to the middle of the opposite side.

easy.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
easy.why: The two lines through the midpoints of opposite sides.

easy.q: Which letter has a vertical line of symmetry?
easy.why: The left half of A mirrors the right half. F, G and R look different on each side.

easy.q: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a square?
easy.why: A square looks the same four times in one full turn.

easy.q: What is the smallest angle by which a regular hexagon can be turned to look the same?

medium.q: What is the smallest angle by which an equilateral triangle can be turned to fit onto itself?
medium.why: It looks the same 3 times in a full turn, so 360° / 3 = 120°.

medium.q: How many lines of symmetry does the capital letter H have?
medium.why: One vertical line and one horizontal line.

medium.q: A paper is folded in half and a hole is punched 3 cm from the fold. After unfolding, how far apart are the two holes?
medium.why: The two holes are mirror images, each 3 cm from the fold, so 6 cm apart.

medium.q: A square paper is folded in half and then in half again. One hole is punched away from the folds. How many holes show after unfolding?
medium.why: Folding twice makes 4 layers, so one punch goes through 4 layers.

medium.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular octagon have?
medium.why: A regular polygon has as many lines of symmetry as sides.

medium.q: Which letter has both a vertical and a horizontal line of symmetry?
medium.why: A has only a vertical line. B and E have only a horizontal line.

hard.q: A paper is folded in half. Two holes are punched, 2 cm and 5 cm from the fold. After unfolding, how far apart are the two farthest holes?
hard.why: There are 4 holes at 2 cm and 5 cm on each side of the fold. The farthest pair is 5 + 5 = 10 cm apart.

hard.q: A regular polygon can be turned by 40° to look the same, and no smaller turn works. How many sides has the polygon?
Think of plain capital letters A to J. How many have a horizontal line of symmetry?
hard.why: B, C, D, E, H and I have a horizontal line. A, F, G and J do not.

hard.q: A circle is divided into 8 equal sectors. They are coloured alternately red and blue. What is the smallest angle by which it can be turned to look the same?
hard.why: The pattern repeats every 2 sectors = 2 x 45° = 90°.

hard.q: A figure has 6 lines of symmetry and looks the same after turns of equal size. What is its smallest angle of rotation?
hard.why: It is like a regular hexagon: 360° / 6 = 60°.

hard.q: Which capital letter has rotational symmetry of order 2 but no line of symmetry?
hard.why: S looks the same after a half turn but its halves do not mirror. H and O have lines of symmetry too.

easy.q: Which is greater, -3 or -7?
easy.why: On the number line -3 is to the right of -7, so it is greater.

easy.q: What is 5 + (-8)?
easy.why: Moving 8 steps left from 5 lands on -3.

easy.q: What number added to -9 gives 0?
easy.why: -9 + 9 = 0, so 9 is the additive inverse of -9.

easy.q: A lift is on floor 4 and goes down 6 floors. Which floor is it on now?
easy.why: 4 - 6 = -2, which is the second floor below ground.

easy.q: Which list shows -5, 2, -1, 0 in order from smallest to largest?
easy.why: Numbers further left on the number line are smaller.
Both numbers go left, so add 6 + 3 = 9 and keep the minus sign.

medium.q: Meena has ₹500 in her account and withdraws ₹750 using an overdraft. What is her balance?
What is 7 - (-5)?
medium.why: Subtracting a negative is adding the positive: 7 + 5 = 12.

medium.q: What is -8 - 6?
medium.why: Start at -8 and move 6 more to the left: -14.

medium.q: What is -3 + 9 - 10?
How many integers lie strictly between -4 and 3?
medium.why: They are -3, -2, -1, 0, 1 and 2.

medium.q: A submarine is at -30 m. It rises 12 m and then dives 25 m. Where is it now?

hard.q: Which three integers add up to -6?
hard.why: -10 + 7 = -3 and -3 + (-3) = -6. The other sets give 0, 0 and -14.

hard.q: A lift starts at floor -2, goes up 9 floors, then down 14 floors, then up 5 floors. On which floor does it stop?

hard.why: Inside the braces: -6 + 2 + 5 = 1. Then -18 - 1 + 3 = -16.

hard.q: At night Leh is at -15°C. By noon the temperature rises 9°C, and by the next night it falls 14°C. What is the temperature then?

easy.q: Choose the correct form: Meena ___ a letter every week.
easy.why: Habit with singular subject: writes.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: He ___ for an hour now.
easy.why: 'For an hour now' needs present perfect continuous.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: We ___ cricket yesterday.
easy.why: Yesterday needs simple past.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: She ___ to Delhi next month.
easy.why: Next month is future.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: I ___ my lunch already.
easy.why: Already + I: have finished.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: Look! It ___.
easy.why: 'Look!' points to what is happening now.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: When I reached, the film ___.
medium.why: Past perfect for the earlier action.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: At 9 p.m. yesterday, I ___ dinner.
medium.why: Past continuous for an action in progress at a past time.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: They ___ here since 2015.
medium.why: 'Since' + a point in time: present perfect.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius.
medium.why: A scientific fact uses simple present.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: By next June, he ___ here for ten years.
medium.why: Future perfect shows completion by a future time.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: Why ___ you late yesterday?
medium.why: Yesterday needs past: were.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: She has been living here since 2020.
She has lived here from 2020 since.
hard.why: 'Since' needs a perfect tense.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: The bell rang before the teacher had entered.
The bell has rung before the teacher entered.
The bell had rung before the teacher entered.
The bell had rung before the teacher enters.
hard.why: The earlier action takes past perfect, the later action takes simple past.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: I wish I know the answer.
I wish I knew the answer.
I wish I will know the answer.
I wish I am knowing the answer.
hard.why: 'Wish' about the present takes the past form.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: I have not seen her since Monday.
I did not see her since Monday.
I have not seen her for Monday.
I am not seeing her since Monday.
hard.why: 'Since' needs present perfect.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: As soon as he will arrive, I will call you.
As soon as he arrived, I will call you.
As soon as he arriving, I call you.
As soon as he arrives, I will call you.
hard.why: In time clauses about the future we use present, not 'will'.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: He always complains about the noise since a week.
He is always complaining about the noise.
hard.why: The continuous with 'always' shows an annoying habit; other options are ungrammatical.

easy.q: Choose the verb: The flowers ___ fresh.
easy.why: Plural flowers: are.

easy.q: Choose the verb: My parents ___ at home.
easy.why: Plural subject.

easy.q: Choose the verb: Sheela ___ a good singer.
easy.why: Singular subject: is.

easy.q: Choose the verb: Gold ___ a precious metal.
easy.why: Gold is singular.

easy.q: Choose the verb: Every boy ___ present today.
easy.why: Every takes a singular verb.

easy.q: Choose the verb: Tom and Jerry ___ friends.
easy.why: Joined by 'and': plural.

medium.q: Choose the verb: The team ___ practising on the ground.
medium.why: The team acts as one unit.

medium.q: Choose the verb: Physics ___ difficult for some.
medium.why: Subjects ending in -ics are singular.

medium.q: Choose the verb: Neither Raj nor his friends ___ late.
medium.why: The verb agrees with the nearer subject, friends.

medium.q: Choose the verb: The principal and teacher ___ coming. (one person)
medium.why: One person with two roles takes a singular verb.

medium.q: Choose the verb: The scissors ___ on the table.
medium.why: Scissors takes a plural verb.

medium.q: Choose the verb: Many a student ___ failed this exam.
medium.why: Many a is followed by a singular noun and verb.

hard.q: Choose the verb: Not only the teacher but also the students ___ present.
hard.why: The verb agrees with the nearer subject.

hard.q: Choose the verb: One of the best players ___ injured.
hard.why: The subject is 'One'.

hard.q: Choose the verb: The quality of the mangoes ___ poor.
hard.why: The subject is 'quality', not 'mangoes'.

hard.q: Choose the verb: Fifty kilometres ___ a long distance to walk.
hard.why: A distance as a whole is singular.

hard.q: Choose the verb: Each of the girls ___ given a prize.
hard.why: Each is singular.

hard.q: Choose the verb: Half of the cake ___ eaten, and half of the biscuits ___ eaten too.
hard.why: The verb agrees with the noun after 'of': cake (singular), biscuits (plural).

easy.q: Choose the modal: ___ I come in, sir? (asking permission)
easy.why: 'May' is used to ask for permission.

easy.q: Choose the modal: Birds ___ fly. (ability)
easy.why: Can shows ability.

easy.q: Choose the modal: You ___ wear a helmet. (rule)
easy.why: Must shows obligation.

easy.q: Choose the word: I need ___ water. (a small quantity)
easy.why: Uncountable water: a little.

easy.q: Choose the word: She has ___ friends. (a large number)
easy.why: Countable plural: many.

easy.q: Choose the word: ___ girl in the class got a prize. (all of them, one by one)
easy.why: Every + singular noun.

medium.q: Choose the modal: He ___ be at home; his lights are on. (probably)
medium.why: Must can express strong probability.

medium.q: Choose the modal: ___ you help me, please? (polite request)
medium.why: Could is a polite request.

medium.q: Choose the modal: You ___ to respect your elders.
medium.why: Ought to shows duty.

medium.q: Choose the word: He gave me ___ advice. (not a number)
medium.why: Advice is uncountable.

medium.q: Choose the word: There were ___ people at the fair, so we left early. (too many)
medium.why: People are countable.

medium.q: Choose the word: ___ of the two roads leads to the village.
medium.why: Either means one of two.

hard.q: Which sentence shows a past habit?
o: We would play in the fields every evening.
We will play in the fields every evening.
We must play in the fields every evening.
We can play in the fields every evening.
hard.why: 'Would' can show past habit.

hard.q: Which sentence shows no need?
hard.why: Needn't means it is not necessary.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: She can't have see the message.
She cannot have seen the message.
She cannot has seen the message.
She can not saw the message.
hard.why: Modal + have + past participle.

hard.q: Which sentence uses the quantifier correctly?
o: Fewer students came than we expected.
Less students came than we expected.
Few students came than we expected.
Lesser students came than we expected.
hard.why: Use fewer with countable nouns.

hard.q: Which sentence shows prohibition?
hard.why: Mustn't = it is forbidden.

hard.q: Which sentence uses 'much' correctly?
hard.why: Time (meaning duration) is uncountable.

easy.q: Change to passive: Ravi writes a letter.
o: A letter was written by Ravi.
A letter is written by Ravi.
easy.why: Simple present passive: is/are + past participle.

easy.q: Which sentence is passive?
o: The window was broken by the ball.
easy.why: The window receives the action.

easy.q: Change to passive: The cat drank the milk.
o: The milk is drunk by the cat.
The milk was drank by the cat.
The milk was drunk by the cat.
easy.why: Simple past passive: was/were + participle.

easy.q: Change to passive: They will build a bridge.
o: A bridge is built by them.
A bridge was built by them.
A bridge will be built by them.
A bridge will built by them.
easy.why: Future passive: will be + participle.

easy.q: Which sentence is active?
o: The wall was painted by Anu.
easy.why: The subject Anu does the action.

easy.q: Change to passive: She sings a song.
o: A song was sung by her.
A song is sing by her.
A song is sung by her.
easy.why: Present passive uses is + participle.

medium.q: Change to passive: The students are cleaning the room.
o: The room is being cleaned by the students.
The room is cleaned by the students.
The room was being cleaned by the students.
The room has been cleaned by the students.
medium.why: Present continuous passive: is being + participle.

medium.q: Change to passive: The teacher was praising the boy.
o: The boy is being praised by the teacher.
The boy was praised by the teacher.
The boy was being praised by the teacher.
The boy has been praised by the teacher.
medium.why: Past continuous passive: was being + participle.

medium.q: Change to passive: Mohan has completed the project.
o: The project is completed by Mohan.
The project has been completed by Mohan.
The project was completed by Mohan.
The project had been completed by Mohan.
medium.why: Present perfect passive: has been + participle.

medium.q: Change to passive: Did Rani break the glass?
o: Was the glass broken by Rani?
Did the glass broken by Rani?
Is the glass broken by Rani?
medium.why: Question in simple past: Was + object + participle.

medium.q: Change to passive: Farmers grow wheat in Punjab.
o: Wheat was grown in Punjab by farmers.
Wheat grows in Punjab by farmers.
Wheat is growing in Punjab by farmers.
Wheat is grown in Punjab by farmers.
medium.why: Simple present passive.

medium.q: Change to passive: Who wrote this poem?
o: By whom was this poem written?
medium.why: Who becomes 'by whom' in the passive.

hard.q: Change to passive: She must finish the work.
o: The work must finish by her.
The work must have been finished by her.
The work must be finished by her.
The work is must finished by her.
hard.why: Modal passive: modal + be + participle.

hard.q: Which sentence cannot be changed into the passive?
hard.why: Intransitive verbs (rose) have no object.

hard.q: Change to passive: Please open the door.
hard.why: An imperative takes 'Let ... be + participle'.

hard.q: Change to passive: People say that he is honest.
o: He is say to be honest.
It said that he is honest.
It is said that he is honest.
It is saying that he is honest.
hard.why: Impersonal passive: It is said that ...

hard.q: Change to passive: He gave me a book.
o: A book gave me by him.
I was given a book by him.
I gave a book by him.
I was gave a book by him.
hard.why: With two objects, either may become the subject; 'was given' is correct.

hard.q: Which is the correct passive of 'We have not finished the exercise'?
o: The exercise has not finished by us.
The exercise is not been finished by us.
The exercise not has been finished by us.
The exercise has not been finished by us.
hard.why: Present perfect passive with not.

easy.q: Choose the word: The class starts ___ Monday.
easy.why: Days take 'on'.

easy.q: Choose the word: The picture hangs ___ the wall.
easy.why: A surface: on.

easy.q: Choose the word: I will see you ___ the evening.
easy.why: Parts of the day take 'in'.

easy.q: Choose the word: I like mangoes ___ I don't like bananas.
easy.why: 'But' shows contrast.

easy.q: Choose the word: He is afraid ___ spiders.
easy.why: 'Afraid of'.

easy.q: Choose the word: He was late ___ the bus broke down.
easy.why: 'Because' gives the reason.

medium.q: Choose the word: The match was postponed ___ rain.
medium.why: 'Because of' is followed by a noun.

medium.q: Choose the word: The Prime Minister is ___ Delhi.
medium.why: In for cities.

medium.q: Choose the word: She is good ___ mathematics.
medium.why: 'Good at'.

medium.q: Choose the word: Study hard ___ you may pass.
medium.why: 'So that' shows purpose.

medium.q: Choose the word: She apologised ___ her mistake.
medium.why: 'Apologise for' is the fixed phrase.

medium.q: Choose the word: ___ he was tired, he finished the race.
medium.why: Although shows contrast.

hard.q: Choose the word: The books are divided ___ the five children.
hard.why: Among is used for more than two.

hard.q: Choose the word: Rohit insisted ___ paying the bill.
hard.why: 'Insist on'.

hard.q: Choose the word: He has been absent ___ Tuesday.
hard.why: Since + a point in time.

hard.q: Choose the word: I won't go ___ you come with me.
hard.why: 'Unless' means 'if not'.

hard.q: Choose the word: The thief escaped ___ the window.
hard.why: Through shows passage.

hard.q: Choose the word: Neither the manager ___ the clerk was present.
hard.why: Neither is followed by nor.

easy.q: Which punctuation mark ends a question?
easy.why: A question mark ends a question.

easy.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: I bought pens, books and bags.
I bought, pens books and bags.
I bought pens books, and bags.
I bought pens, books, and, bags.
easy.why: Commas separate items in a list.

easy.q: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
easy.why: Capital letter and full stop.

easy.q: Arrange to form a sentence: school / goes / to / Raj
easy.why: Subject, verb, then place.

easy.q: Choose the correct sentence.
easy.why: It's = it is.

easy.q: Arrange: the / is / flying / kite
easy.why: Standard word order.

medium.q: Which is punctuated correctly?
medium.why: The comma goes inside the quotation marks.

medium.q: Choose the correct sentence.
medium.why: Exclamation then the second sentence.

medium.q: Where should the apostrophe go? 'the girls books' (one girl)
medium.why: One girl owns: 's.

medium.q: Arrange: was / by / the / letter / written / Neha
o: The letter was written by Neha.
Neha written was the letter by.
Was the letter by Neha written.
Written by the letter Neha was.
medium.why: Passive order.

medium.q: Choose the correct use of colon: You need three things
o: You need: three things a pen, a pencil and a ruler.
You need three: things a pen, a pencil, and a ruler.
You need three things a pen: a pencil and a ruler.
You need three things: a pen, a pencil and a ruler.
medium.why: A colon introduces a list after a complete clause.

medium.q: Arrange: early / the / reached / station / we
medium.why: Subject, verb, object, adverb.

hard.q: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
hard.why: The question mark goes inside the quotation marks for a quoted question.

hard.q: Which sentence uses a hyphen correctly?
hard.why: Compound adjective takes a hyphen.

hard.q: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?
o: It was; raining we stayed inside.
It was raining; and, we stayed inside.
It was raining we; stayed inside.
It was raining; we stayed inside.
hard.why: A semicolon joins two linked complete clauses.

hard.q: Which order gives a meaningful sentence? P: after school Q: Sunil played R: cricket S: and returned home
hard.why: Q R P S reads: Sunil played cricket after school and returned home.

hard.q: Choose the correct sentence.
hard.why: Who's = who is.

hard.q: Which is the best order? 1. He packed his bag. 2. The alarm rang. 3. He woke up. 4. He left for school.
hard.why: Alarm, waking, packing, leaving.

easy.q: Choose the synonym of 'tiny'.
easy.why: Tiny means very small.

easy.q: Choose the correct word: I can't ___ the noise. (bear/bare)
easy.why: Bear = tolerate.

easy.q: Choose the antonym of 'brave'.
easy.why: Cowardly is the opposite.

easy.q: Choose the phrasal verb meaning 'continue': Keep ___.
easy.why: 'Keep on' = continue.

easy.q: Choose the correct word: The ___ was blowing hard. (wind/wined)
easy.why: Wind is moving air.

easy.q: Choose the antonym of 'accept'.
easy.why: Refuse is the opposite.

medium.q: Choose the synonym of 'assist'.
medium.why: Assist means help.

medium.q: Choose the correct word: He gave a good ___ for his late arrival. (excuse/excuses)
medium.why: Excuse (noun, singular) fits.

medium.q: Choose the antonym of 'increase'.
medium.why: Decrease is opposite.

medium.q: Choose the meaning of 'give up'.
medium.why: Give up = stop trying.

medium.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'outcome'.
medium.why: Outcome means result.

medium.q: Choose the meaning of 'break the ice'.
medium.why: It means to ease tension and begin talking.

hard.q: Choose the synonym of 'diligent'.
hard.why: Diligent means hardworking.

hard.q: Choose the right word: She is very ___ of her success. (proud/prowd)
hard.why: Proud is the adjective.

hard.q: Choose the antonym of 'scarce'.
hard.why: Plentiful is the opposite of scarce.

hard.q: Choose the meaning of 'look into'.
hard.why: Look into = investigate.

hard.q: Choose the correct word: The weather will ___ our plan. (effect/affect)
hard.why: Affect = influence (verb).

hard.q: Choose the meaning of 'once in a blue moon'.
hard.why: The idiom means very rarely.
