easy.q: Meena wants to know if a claim in science is true. What is the best thing to do?
o: Ask the loudest person in the class
Test it with an experiment and note the results
Read it again and again until it feels true
Accept it because it is in an old book
easy.why: Science checks ideas by observing and testing, not by who says them.

easy.q: After rain, Arjun asks why the puddle in his lane vanished by evening. This habit of asking questions is called
easy.why: Curiosity, asking why and how, is where science begins.

easy.q: Which of these will make a bulb glow when joined in a circuit with a cell and wires?
easy.why: Iron is a conductor of electricity; wood, rubber and plastic are insulators.

easy.q: Which of these changes cannot be reversed?
easy.why: Burning makes new substances such as ash, so the paper cannot be got back.

easy.q: Long ago, people used the shadow of a stick or pillar to find the time of day. Such a device is called a
easy.why: A sundial reads time from the position of a shadow cast by the Sun.

easy.q: Which of these gives out its own light?
easy.why: A candle is a source of light; the others only reflect light that falls on them.

medium.q: Gita tests four things in a circuit with a cell, a bulb and wires: a steel spoon, an eraser, an iron key and a plastic comb. Which pair makes the bulb glow?
medium.why: Metals like steel and iron conduct electricity; the eraser and plastic comb do not.

medium.q: Ravi says, "Science is only memorising facts from books." Which reply is best?
o: He is right, since all science is already known
Science is only done by adults in labs
Science also means asking questions and testing ideas by observing and experimenting
medium.why: Science grows through questions, observation and experiments, not just facts.

medium.q: Ice cream melting on a hot day and a cake baking in an oven are both changes. Which statement is correct?
o: Melting can be undone by cooling, but baking a cake cannot be undone
Baking can be undone by cooling the cake
medium.why: Cooling makes the melted ice cream solid again; a baked cake has new substances and cannot return to batter.

medium.q: The length of your shadow changes through the day. What can this help early people do?
o: Roughly tell the time of day
medium.why: As the Sun moves across the sky, shadow length and direction change in a regular way.

medium.q: A student sorts copper wire, chalk, aluminium foil and glass. Which two will conduct electricity?
medium.why: Copper and aluminium are metals and conduct electricity; chalk and glass do not.

medium.q: An experiment gives a result different from your guess. What is the best scientific response?
o: Change the result to match your guess
Check the method, repeat the test and accept what the evidence shows
medium.why: Evidence decides what is true; a guess that fails is still useful learning.

hard.q: A student finds that a graphite pencil lead lets a bulb glow, but wood does not. Which conclusion is correct?
o: Some non-metals, such as graphite, can conduct electricity
Wood is a better conductor than graphite
hard.why: Graphite is a non-metal that conducts, so conductors are not always metals.

hard.q: Sugar is heated in a pan. It melts, turns brown and smells burnt. On cooling it forms a hard black lump. Which conclusion is correct?
o: It is only melting, so sugar can be got back
The colour change is the only change
A new substance has formed, so the change cannot be reversed
hard.why: Browning and the burnt smell show a new substance, so this change is irreversible.

hard.q: Early people noticed that the Moon's shape repeats in about 29 to 30 days. How could this help them?
o: They could stop the Moon changing
They could count months and plan festivals and farming
They could make the Moon brighter
hard.why: A regular pattern in the sky works as a natural calendar.

hard.q: Sita wants to test whether a wider dish makes water dry faster. Which set-up is a fair test?
o: Same amount of water in a wide and a narrow dish, kept in the same place
A wide dish in the sun and a narrow dish in the shade
More water in the wide dish and less in the narrow dish
Wide dish near a fan and narrow dish in a cupboard
hard.why: A fair test changes only one thing; everything else must stay the same.

hard.q: Kabir throws a thick paper plane and a thin one and says thicker paper flies farther. The thick plane was also thrown harder. What is wrong?
o: He changed two things at once, so the result is not a fair comparison
He should not have thrown the thin plane
hard.why: Both paper thickness and throwing force differed, so we cannot tell which one caused the result.

hard.q: A battery runs down in a toy car. Which explanation is best?
o: The battery is only resting and will fully recover
Chemicals inside have been used up and cannot be restored by us simply
hard.why: The chemical change inside a cell uses up its materials, so it is not simply reversible.

easy.q: A drop of lemon juice is put on blue litmus paper. The paper turns
easy.why: Acids turn blue litmus red; lemon juice is acidic.

easy.q: A solution turns red litmus paper blue. The solution is
easy.why: Bases turn red litmus blue.

easy.q: Which of these is acidic?
easy.why: Vinegar contains acetic acid; the other three are basic.

easy.q: Turmeric paper turns red when dipped in
easy.why: Turmeric turns red with bases such as soap solution; it stays yellow in acids and neutral liquids.

easy.q: When an acid and a base mix and cancel each other's effect, the reaction is called
easy.why: Neutralisation is the reaction between an acid and a base.

easy.q: Red rose extract turns green with a
easy.why: Rose extract turns green in bases such as soap solution and dark pink in acids.

medium.q: An ant bite stings because of an acid. Which of these gives relief?
o: Rubbing lemon juice on the spot
Rubbing moist baking soda on the spot
medium.why: A base like baking soda neutralises the acid; vinegar and lemon add more acid.

medium.q: A liquid does not change the colour of red litmus or blue litmus. The liquid is
medium.why: Neutral substances change neither red nor blue litmus.

medium.q: Why does an antacid tablet give relief from acidity?
o: It is acidic and adds more acid
It is basic and neutralises the extra acid in the stomach
It is neutral and does nothing
medium.why: Antacids contain bases that neutralise excess acid.

medium.q: A farmer's soil is too acidic for his crop. What can he add to treat it?
medium.why: A base such as slaked lime neutralises acidic soil.

medium.q: A secret note is written with baking soda solution on white paper. Which liquid brushed over it shows the message?
medium.why: Baking soda is basic and turns yellow turmeric red.

medium.q: Tube A turns blue litmus red and does not affect red litmus. Tube B turns red litmus blue and does not affect blue litmus. Tube C changes neither. Which is correct?
o: A is basic, B is acidic, C is neutral
A is neutral, B is acidic, C is basic
A is acidic, B is neutral, C is basic
A is acidic, B is basic, C is neutral
medium.why: Acids turn blue litmus red, bases turn red litmus blue, and neutral substances change neither.

hard.q: Rose extract turns liquid X green, so X is basic. Excess amla juice (an acid) is slowly added to X. What is the likely colour change?
o: Green changes to pink or red
It becomes colourless first and stays so
hard.why: Acid cancels the base and then makes the mixture acidic, so rose extract turns pink or red.

hard.q: A beaker becomes warm when an acid and a base are mixed. Which is the best explanation?
o: Mixing any two liquids warms them
Neutralisation releases heat while forming salt and water
hard.why: Neutralisation gives off heat and forms salt and water.

hard.q: Grape juice shows red with rose extract. A lot of baking soda is added in small amounts. What will rose extract show in the end?
o: It becomes red then pink then red
It turns green once enough soda is added
hard.why: Baking soda is basic: it first neutralises the juice and, in excess, makes the mixture basic.

hard.q: A blindfolded student must tell an acid from a base. Which indicator can she use without seeing colours?
o: Onion strips, whose smell vanishes in a base
hard.why: Onion and vanilla smells change in bases, so smell can be the indicator.

hard.q: A student tests a liquid with turmeric paper, sees no change and says it is neutral. Why is this wrong?
o: Turmeric changes colour in neutral liquids
Turmeric also stays yellow in acids, so the liquid could be acidic
hard.why: Only bases change turmeric, so another indicator like litmus is needed to separate acids and neutral liquids.

hard.q: A factory releases acidic waste water into a lake. What can be added to treat it?
hard.why: A base neutralises the acid.

easy.q: How many terminals does an electric cell have?
easy.why: A cell has a positive and a negative terminal.

easy.q: The metal cap on one end of a cell is its
easy.why: The metal cap is the positive terminal; the flat end is negative.

easy.q: A lamp in a simple circuit glows only when the switch is
easy.why: A closed switch completes the circuit so current can flow.

easy.q: Two or more cells joined together are called a
easy.why: A battery is a group of cells connected together.

easy.q: In the symbol for a cell, the longer line stands for the
easy.why: The longer line is positive and the shorter, thicker line is negative.

easy.q: Which part of a lamp glows when current passes through it?
easy.why: The thin wire inside, the filament, heats up and glows.

medium.q: A gap is left between two wires in a circuit with a cell and a lamp. Which object placed in the gap makes the lamp glow?
medium.why: Steel is a conductor; the others are insulators.

medium.q: A torch lamp glows when its switch is pushed forward but not when it is pushed back. Why?
o: Pushing forward completes the circuit and pushing back breaks it
The cell is full in one position
medium.why: A switch closes or opens the gap in the circuit.

medium.q: How should two cells be joined to make a battery in a torch?
o: Positive terminal of one to negative terminal of the other
medium.why: In a battery, cells are joined one after the other with unlike terminals touching.

medium.q: Neha leaves the plastic covering on the wire ends that touch the cell. The cell and lamp are fine, but the lamp does not glow. Why?
o: Plastic is an insulator and blocks the current
Wires need no covering to glow
medium.why: Current cannot pass through the plastic, so the circuit is not complete.

medium.q: A lamp, cell and switch are connected, the switch is on and the cell is good, but the lamp does not glow. What is a likely cause?
o: The wire is made of copper
medium.why: A broken filament means the circuit is open at the lamp.

medium.q: An LED does not glow when connected to a cell, but glows when the connections to the cell are swapped. Why?
o: An LED works only when connected the correct way round
medium.why: An LED allows current in one direction only.

hard.q: Two lamps are joined one after the other in a single loop with a cell. One filament breaks. What happens to the other lamp?
o: It also goes off because the loop is broken
hard.why: In a single loop, a break anywhere stops the current everywhere.

hard.q: A cell, a lamp and two switches S1 and S2 are all joined one after another in one loop. When will the lamp glow?
o: Only when both switches are closed
hard.why: Both switches must be closed to complete the loop.

hard.q: A student's circuit does not work. Which is NOT a likely cause?
o: A wire end is not touching a terminal
The glass of the lamp is transparent
hard.why: A transparent bulb is normal and does not stop the current.

hard.q: A cell is joined to lamp A with its own switch and to lamp B with its own switch, so that each lamp has a separate path. Only A's switch is closed. What happens?
o: A glows and B stays off
B glows and A stays off
hard.why: Each lamp has its own path, so closing one switch lights only that lamp.

hard.q: What is the best material choice for an electric switch?
o: Plastic contacts inside and a metal cover outside
Rubber contacts and a wooden cover
Metal contacts and a metal cover
Metal contacts inside and a plastic cover outside
hard.why: Metal lets current pass in the circuit, and plastic protects the user.

hard.q: A student places a steel spoon, a rubber band, a pencil lead, chalk and a plastic pen cap one at a time in a gap in a circuit. Which pair makes the lamp glow?
hard.why: Steel and graphite conduct electricity; rubber, chalk and plastic do not.

easy.q: The property that lets metals be beaten into thin sheets is called
easy.why: Malleable metals can be hammered into sheets, like aluminium foil.

easy.q: Which property allows copper to be drawn into thin wires?
easy.why: Ductile materials can be stretched into wires.

easy.q: A school bell is made of metal because metals
o: produce a ringing sound when struck
easy.why: This ringing property is called sonority.

easy.q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
easy.why: Mercury is the only common metal that is liquid at room temperature.

easy.q: The brown flaky layer on an iron gate left in rain is called
easy.why: Iron reacts with air and moisture to form rust.

easy.q: Which non-metal is used to purify drinking water?
easy.why: Chlorine kills germs in water.

medium.q: Which cheap metal is rolled into thin foldable sheets to wrap food?
medium.why: Aluminium is malleable, light and cheap.

medium.q: The handle of a cooking pan is made of plastic because plastic
o: is a good conductor of heat
is a poor conductor of heat
medium.why: A poor conductor keeps the handle from getting hot.

medium.q: Why are gold and silver good for making ornaments?
o: They shine, can be shaped easily and do not rust quickly
medium.why: Lustre, malleability and corrosion resistance make them suitable.

medium.q: Magnesium burns in air to form a white powder. Its solution in water will turn
medium.why: Metal oxides are generally basic.

medium.q: Sulfur burns to form a gas. When it dissolves in water, the solution
medium.why: Non-metal oxides are generally acidic.

medium.q: Which iron nail will rust fastest after a week?
o: One kept in tap water open to air
One in dry air with a drying agent
medium.why: Rusting needs both air and moisture.

hard.q: Nail A is coated with oil, nail B is in water and nail C is in vinegar, all in the open. Which will rust least?
o: A, because oil keeps out air and water
hard.why: Oil blocks air and water.

hard.q: Why does an ironsmith heat iron red-hot before hammering it?
o: Heat makes iron softer, so it is easier to shape
Heat stops iron being a metal
hard.why: Hot iron is more malleable.

hard.q: Why does painting an iron gate prevent rusting?
o: The paint changes iron into copper
The paint separates the iron from air and moisture
The paint removes oxygen from air
hard.why: Rusting needs air and moisture.

hard.q: Why are aluminium wires used in overhead power lines?
o: It is a good conductor, light and can be drawn into wires
hard.why: Good conduction, low weight and ductility make aluminium suitable.

hard.q: A student hits a lump of coal and a copper piece with a hammer. The coal breaks, the copper flattens. Conclusion?
o: Coal is brittle and copper is malleable
hard.why: Non-metals like coal are brittle; metals are malleable.

hard.q: X is shiny, can be drawn into wires and rings when struck. Y is dull and crumbles on hitting. Z is a shiny liquid. Which are metals?
hard.why: Shine, ductility and sonority are metal properties, and mercury is a liquid metal.

easy.q: Melting of ice is a
easy.why: No new substance forms when ice melts.

easy.q: Rusting of an iron gate is a
easy.why: Rust is a new substance.

easy.q: Which is a chemical change?
easy.why: Burning makes ash and gases.

easy.q: Lime water turns milky when which gas passes through?
easy.why: Carbon dioxide reacts with lime water.

easy.q: Which does NOT form a new substance?
easy.why: Dissolving is physical.

easy.q: Burning a substance in air with heat and light is called
easy.why: Combustion is burning.

medium.q: Milk turns to curd. This is a
o: chemical change, as new substances form
medium.why: Curd cannot become milk.

medium.q: Which pair has two physical changes?
o: Dissolving salt in water and freezing water
medium.why: Dissolving and freezing give no new substance; rusting, burning, curdling and baking do.

medium.q: Burning magnesium ribbon gives a white powder. Why is it chemical?
o: A new substance, a white powder, forms
medium.why: The white powder is magnesium oxide, a new substance, so the change is chemical.

medium.q: Vinegar is added to baking soda. A gas forms that turns lime water milky. The gas is
medium.why: Baking soda and vinegar react to give carbon dioxide, which turns lime water milky.

medium.q: Candle wax near the flame melts and hardens again. This is
medium.why: Only the state changes between solid and liquid; no new substance forms.

medium.q: Which can be reversed?
medium.why: Freezing is a change of state and can be undone by warming; the others make new substances.

hard.q: Of boiling water, rusting, baking bread and crushing chalk, how many are chemical?
hard.why: Rusting and baking make new substances; boiling and crushing do not.

hard.q: A candle burns. Which statement is correct?
o: Wax melting is physical, wick and vapour burning is chemical
hard.why: The melting of wax is physical, while burning of the wick and wax vapour is chemical.

hard.q: Rocks crack from heating and cooling, while acid rain slowly dissolves limestone. These are
hard.why: Cracking is physical; dissolving by acid is chemical.

hard.q: Vegetable peels become compost in a pit. This is
o: a chemical change that cannot be reversed
hard.why: Rotting makes new substances, so the change is chemical and not reversible.

hard.q: Which mixture will turn lime water milky?
hard.why: Only vinegar with baking soda gives carbon dioxide, which turns lime water milky.

hard.q: Why can a boiled egg not become raw again?
o: Heat caused a chemical change forming new substances
hard.why: Heat changes the egg's substances permanently, so it cannot be raw again.

easy.q: The bump in a boy's throat appears because of growth of the
easy.why: The voice box grows and the voice deepens.

easy.q: Chemicals that regulate growth in the body are called
easy.why: Hormones are chemical messengers that control growth and changes.

easy.q: The monthly discharge of blood in girls is called
easy.why: Menstruation is the monthly discharge of blood in girls during reproductive maturity.

easy.q: Pimples appear in adolescence mainly because
easy.why: Hormones make oil glands more active, which can block skin pores.

easy.q: The stage when the body becomes able to reproduce is
easy.why: Puberty is when the body becomes able to reproduce.

easy.q: Which should teenagers stay away from?
easy.why: Tobacco harms health and can cause addiction.

medium.q: Which change occurs in both boys and girls?
medium.why: Hair under the arms grows in both boys and girls; the other changes are specific to one.

medium.q: Which meal is best for a growing teenager?
medium.why: Growing teenagers need all nutrients, which a balanced meal provides.

medium.q: Which is a good hygiene habit during periods?
o: Change pads regularly and wash hands
medium.why: Regular changing and washing hands prevents infection.

medium.q: A boy's voice becomes deep as his
medium.why: The growing voice box deepens a boy's voice.

medium.q: A friend sends hurtful messages online. What should you do?
medium.why: Cyberbullying is harmful, and a trusted adult can help stop it.

medium.q: Priya feels happy then irritable in a day. This is
medium.why: Hormonal changes in the teenage years cause mood swings.

hard.q: A girl has a swelling in the neck. A doctor suspects lack of
hard.why: Lack of iodine can enlarge the thyroid gland in the neck, which needs a doctor's advice.

hard.q: Shalu says adolescence brings only physical changes. A better statement is
o: Emotional and social changes also occur
hard.why: Adolescence brings physical, emotional and social changes.

hard.q: Raju says trying tobacco once is harmless as he can quit anytime. Why wrong?
hard.why: Harmful substances can lead to addiction, so even one try is risky.

hard.q: Which statement about adolescence is incorrect?
o: It is a stage of growth
It starts at the same age in everyone
hard.why: Adolescence starts at different ages for different people.

hard.q: Asha's height shot up but her classmate Rani has not grown. This shows
hard.why: Adolescent growth starts at different ages in different people, which is normal.

hard.q: Friends press Dev to try a harmful substance. Best response?
o: Say no firmly and tell a trusted adult
hard.why: Saying no and telling an adult protects you from addiction.

easy.q: A steel spoon kept in hot tea becomes hot at the other end. Heat travels in the spoon by
easy.why: In solids heat passes from particle to particle without the material moving, which is conduction.

easy.q: Smoke from a chimney goes up because
o: hot air is lighter and rises
easy.why: Warm air is lighter and rises; this movement is convection.

easy.q: Heat from the Sun reaches us mainly by
easy.why: Radiation needs no medium, so it crosses empty space from the Sun.

easy.q: Which of these is a poor conductor of heat?
easy.why: Wood is a poor conductor; metals are good conductors.

easy.q: Water vapour changing to tiny droplets that form clouds is called
easy.why: Cooling vapour condenses into droplets that form clouds.

easy.q: Which clothes are most suitable in summer?
easy.why: Light colours absorb less heat from sunlight than dark colours.

medium.q: On a sunny afternoon at a seaside town, the breeze blows
o: from the land to the sea
from the sea to the land
medium.why: Land warms faster in the day; warm air over land rises and cooler air from the sea flows in.

medium.q: Woollen clothes keep us warm in winter because wool
medium.why: Wool traps air, which is a poor conductor, so body heat does not escape.

medium.q: When water is heated in a pan on a stove, hot water at the bottom moves up. This is
medium.why: Heated water rises and cooler water sinks, setting up convection currents.

medium.q: Why are hollow bricks used in the outer walls in hot places?
o: Air trapped inside slows heat entering
Air inside is a good conductor
medium.why: Air trapped in the hollows is a poor conductor, so less heat enters.

medium.q: Water from rain seeps fastest into
medium.why: Sand has larger gaps between grains, so water seeps through quickly.

medium.q: Water leaving leaves as vapour is called
medium.why: Transpiration is loss of water vapour from leaves.

hard.q: Where is a smoke detector best fitted in a room?
hard.why: Hot smoke rises, so a detector near the ceiling senses it first.

hard.q: An incense stick points downward. The smoke from its burning tip will
hard.why: Hot smoke is lighter than surrounding air, so it rises whichever way the stick points.

hard.q: A glass of lassi is placed inside a larger glass, leaving an air gap. Compared with a single glass, it
o: stays cool longer because the air gap is a poor conductor
hard.why: The air gap is a poor conductor, so heat enters the lassi slowly.

hard.q: At night in a coastal town, the breeze blows
o: from the sea to the land
from the land to the sea
hard.why: At night land cools faster than sea; warm air rises over the sea and cooler land air moves in to replace it.

hard.q: A city with concrete roads floods more than a village with soil. Why?
o: Concrete lets little rainwater seep in
hard.why: Concrete lets very little water seep in, so rainwater runs off and floods roads.

hard.q: Which pair is correctly matched?
o: Hot ladle handle: conduction; warmth felt from soup surface: radiation
Hot ladle handle: radiation; warmth felt from soup surface: conduction
hard.why: Heat moves along the metal handle by conduction and across air from the soup surface by radiation.

easy.q: The SI unit of time is the
easy.why: The second is the SI unit.

easy.q: Speed is calculated as
easy.why: Speed = distance / time.

easy.q: The time a pendulum takes for one complete to-and-fro swing is its
easy.why: Time period is time for one oscillation.

easy.q: The SI unit of speed is
easy.why: Distance in metres over time in seconds.

easy.q: An object moving in a straight line covering equal distances in equal times shows
easy.why: Uniform means constant speed.

easy.q: Which device records the distance travelled by a vehicle?
easy.why: An odometer counts distance.

medium.q: A car covers 150 km in 3 hours. Its speed is
A bus must cover 240 km at 60 km/h. The time taken is
A train runs at 20 m/s. In km/h this is
A cyclist rides at 6 m/s for 5 minutes. The distance covered is
A pendulum completes 20 oscillations in 40 s. Its time period is
Anu runs 100 m in 14 s and Bina runs 100 m in 12.5 s. Who is faster?
medium.why: Bina takes less time for the same distance: 100/12.5 = 8 m/s against about 7.1 m/s for Anu.

hard.q: A car runs at 90 km/h. Its speed in m/s is
A toy covers 5 m, 5 m, 5 m and 8 m in four successive seconds. Which is correct?
o: Its motion is non-uniform because the last distance differs
hard.why: Equal distances in equal times are needed for uniform motion; the last second differs.

hard.q: A bus travels 60 km in the first hour and 40 km in the next 2 hours. Its average speed is
hard.why: Average speed = total distance / total time = 100 km / 3 h = 33.3 km/h.

hard.q: A train goes at 54 km/h and a cyclist at 16 m/s. Which is faster?
A pendulum has a time period of 1.5 s. The number of oscillations in 3 minutes is
A train covers 150 km in 2 hours 30 minutes. Its speed in m/s is about

easy.q: Saliva in the mouth begins the digestion of
easy.why: Saliva has an enzyme that acts on starch.

easy.q: The longest part of our digestive system is the
easy.why: The small intestine is about 6 metres long.

easy.q: Cows chewing food again after swallowing it is called
easy.why: The food brought back is called cud.

easy.q: The tiny air sacs in lungs where gases are exchanged are called
easy.why: Gas exchange occurs in alveoli.

easy.q: The gas that turns lime water milky is present in larger amount in
easy.why: Exhaled air has more CO2.

easy.q: Most water is absorbed from undigested food in the
easy.why: The large intestine absorbs water.

medium.q: When we breathe in, the diaphragm
o: moves up and chest becomes smaller
moves down and chest space increases
medium.why: Downward diaphragm increases chest volume.

medium.q: Blood carries digested food and oxygen to
medium.why: Blood carries food and oxygen to every cell of the body.

medium.q: Fish breathe using their
medium.why: Gills take oxygen from water.

medium.q: Which statement shows the difference between breathing and respiration?
o: Breathing moves air in and out; respiration releases energy from food in cells
medium.why: Breathing is the movement of air; respiration is the chemical release of energy in cells.

medium.q: Chewing a piece of chapati for a long time makes it taste sweet because
medium.why: Saliva contains an enzyme that breaks starch into sugar, which tastes sweet.

medium.q: An earthworm breathes through its
medium.why: Moist skin allows gas exchange.

hard.q: Birds have no teeth. Which organ grinds their food?
hard.why: Gizzard grinds with swallowed stones.

hard.q: After running, we breathe faster because
o: muscle cells need more oxygen to release energy
hard.why: Working muscles need more energy, so cells need more oxygen and we breathe faster.

hard.q: A frog's tadpole breathes with gills. The adult frog uses
hard.why: A tadpole breathes with gills in water; the adult frog breathes with lungs and through its moist skin.

hard.q: Why do cows chew cud?
o: Grass is tough, so partly digested food is chewed again
hard.why: Grass is tough, so a cow chews the partly digested cud again to digest it fully.

hard.q: A frog kept in a dry place has trouble because
o: its skin must stay moist to take in oxygen
hard.why: A frog takes in oxygen through its skin, which works only when the skin is moist.

hard.q: A student blows through a straw into lime water for a while and it turns milky. This shows
hard.why: Carbon dioxide turns lime water milky, so our breath must contain it.

easy.q: The process by which green plants make their own food using sunlight is called
easy.why: Plants combine carbon dioxide and water using sunlight to make food.

easy.q: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
easy.why: Carbon dioxide enters leaves and is used to make food.

easy.q: Which gas is released by plants during photosynthesis?
easy.why: Oxygen is a by-product of making food.

easy.q: The green pigment that traps sunlight in leaves is
easy.why: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy for photosynthesis.

easy.q: The tiny openings on the surface of leaves are called
easy.why: Gases and water vapour pass through stomata.

easy.q: Xylem vessels carry
o: water and minerals from roots to leaves
easy.why: Xylem carries water and minerals upward.

medium.q: Which part of a plant absorbs water and minerals from the soil?
medium.why: Roots take water and minerals from the soil.

medium.q: Phloem carries
o: food made in the leaves to other parts
medium.why: Phloem moves prepared food to all parts of the plant.

medium.q: A leaf kept in sunlight is boiled in alcohol and tested with iodine. A blue-black colour shows
medium.why: Iodine turns blue-black with starch, a product of photosynthesis.

medium.q: Which statement about plant respiration is correct?
o: Plants take in oxygen and give out carbon dioxide, day and night
Plants take in carbon dioxide only
medium.why: All living cells respire all the time.

medium.q: A potted plant is kept in complete darkness for 36 hours and a leaf is tested with iodine. The leaf
medium.why: In darkness there is no photosynthesis, so no starch is stored.

medium.q: A variegated leaf has green and white patches. After sunlight and an iodine test, which patches turn blue-black?
medium.why: Chlorophyll is needed for photosynthesis, so only green patches make starch.

hard.q: Which pair correctly gives the inputs of photosynthesis?
o: Carbon dioxide and water, with sunlight
hard.why: Plants use carbon dioxide, water and light to make food.

hard.q: Water rises from roots to the leaves of a tall tree mainly because
o: water evaporating from leaves pulls more water up through xylem
hard.why: Loss of water from leaves pulls water up.

hard.q: A polythene bag is tied over a leafy branch in sunshine. Droplets collect inside after a few hours because
o: the leaves lose water vapour through stomata
hard.why: Water vapour from leaves condenses on the cool bag.

hard.q: In bright sunlight, a plant's net gas exchange shows more oxygen released than used. Why?
o: Photosynthesis makes more oxygen than respiration uses
hard.why: Photosynthesis happens only in light, while respiration is continuous.

hard.q: A water plant in a jar gives off many bubbles in sunlight but few in shade. The bubbles are mostly
hard.why: More light means more photosynthesis, so more oxygen.

hard.q: A ring of bark is removed from a stem. Over days, the stem swells just above the ring because
o: food from leaves piles up where phloem is cut
hard.why: The phloem carrying food downward is blocked.

easy.q: An object that gives out its own light is called
easy.why: Luminous objects such as the Sun make their own light.

easy.q: We see the Moon because it
easy.why: The Moon does not make light; it reflects sunlight.

easy.q: Light travels in
easy.why: Light travels in straight lines, which is why shadows have sharp edges.

easy.q: Which material is opaque?
easy.why: Wood blocks light; clear glass, air and clean water let it pass.

easy.q: Frosted glass lets some light through but we cannot see clearly. It is
easy.why: Frosted glass lets light through but scatters it, so it is translucent.

easy.q: In a plane mirror, the left-right swap in the image is called
easy.why: A plane mirror swaps left and right, which is called lateral inversion.

medium.q: Which three things are needed to form a shadow?
o: Source of light, opaque object and screen
medium.why: A shadow forms when an opaque object blocks light.

medium.q: A periscope uses
o: two plane mirrors fixed at 45 degrees
medium.why: Two mirrors at 45 degrees turn light twice, letting you see over obstacles.

medium.q: A ray of light falls on a plane mirror at 40 degrees to the normal. The reflected ray makes with the normal an angle of
medium.why: The angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence, so it is 40 degrees.

medium.q: The word AMBULANCE is written reversed on its front so that
o: it reads correctly in a driver's mirror
medium.why: The reversed word looks correct in the rear-view mirror of the driver ahead because of lateral inversion.

medium.q: The image formed by a pinhole camera is
medium.why: Rays from the top of an object pass the hole and reach the bottom of the screen, giving an inverted image.

medium.q: A torch is moved closer to a book on a table in a dark room. The book's shadow on the wall
medium.why: A source nearer the object blocks more light angles, so a bigger shadow forms.

hard.q: Between a lamp and a wall, a student places cardboard, wax paper and clear glass one at a time. The shadows are
hard.why: Opaque cardboard gives a dark shadow, wax paper a faint one, and clear glass almost none.

hard.q: In a periscope, the two mirrors are placed
o: parallel to each other, each at 45 degrees to the tube
hard.why: Mirrors parallel at 45 degrees turn the light twice so you see over a wall.

hard.q: We cannot see the shadow of a bird flying very high because
o: the shadow falls far away and becomes faint and spread out
hard.why: The shadow falls very far from the bird, so it is faint and spread out.

hard.q: The pinhole of a pinhole camera is made larger. The image becomes
hard.why: A bigger hole lets more light in, but rays spread, so the image is brighter yet blurred.

hard.q: Sunlight through tree leaves makes round bright patches on the ground because
o: small gaps work like pinholes forming round images of the Sun
hard.why: Each small gap acts as a pinhole and makes a round image of the Sun.

hard.q: A boy's shadow is longer at 4 pm than at noon because
o: the Sun is lower in the sky
hard.why: When the Sun is lower in the sky, shadows are longer.

easy.q: Day and night happen because the Earth
o: moves around the Sun in a day
moves closer to and away from the Sun
easy.why: As Earth spins, the half facing the Sun has day while the other half has night.

easy.q: The Earth completes one rotation in about
easy.why: Earth takes about 24 hours for one rotation, which makes one day and night.

easy.q: The Earth completes one revolution around the Sun in about
easy.why: The Earth takes about 365 days.

easy.q: The path of the Earth around the Sun is called its
easy.why: Earth's fixed path around the Sun is called its orbit.

easy.q: A solar eclipse happens when the
o: Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth
Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon
Sun comes between the Earth and the Moon
easy.why: The Moon passes between the Sun and Earth and blocks sunlight.

easy.q: A lunar eclipse happens when the
o: Moon is between the Sun and the Earth
Earth is between the Sun and the Moon
Sun is between the Earth and the Moon
Moon is farthest from the Earth
easy.why: Earth's shadow falls on the Moon when Earth lies between the Sun and Moon.

medium.q: Seasons change mainly because
o: Earth's axis is tilted as it goes around the Sun
Earth moves nearer to the Sun in summer
the Sun moves up and down
medium.why: The tilt changes how much sunlight each hemisphere gets during the year.

medium.q: The Sun seems to rise in the east because
o: the Sun really moves around the Earth
Earth rotates from west to east
the Earth goes around the Sun in a day
medium.why: Earth spins from west to east, so the Sun only appears to move from east to west.

medium.q: A leap year has an extra day because
o: Earth spins slower every fourth year
Earth takes about 365 1/4 days to go around the Sun
medium.why: The extra quarter days add up to one day every four years, added as 29 February.

medium.q: It is safe to watch a lunar eclipse with the eyes but not a solar eclipse because
o: the Moon is too hot to look at
a lunar eclipse is much brighter
a lunar eclipse happens only in the day
the Sun's light can damage the eyes even when it is partly hidden
medium.why: Looking at the Sun can damage the eyes, while the eclipsed Moon is not harmful to view.

medium.q: The stars seem to move across the night sky because
o: stars revolve around Earth every night
medium.why: Earth's spin makes stars appear to drift across the sky.

medium.q: Different stars are seen in different months because
o: stars move to new places each month
the Sun moves across the stars
medium.why: As Earth goes around the Sun, the night side faces different stars in different months.

hard.q: Which pairing is right?
o: Solar eclipse on new moon day; lunar eclipse on full moon day
Solar on full moon; lunar on new moon
hard.why: A solar eclipse needs the Moon between Sun and Earth (new moon); a lunar eclipse needs Earth between (full moon).

hard.q: If Earth's axis were not tilted, then
o: there would be no day and night
it would be summer everywhere all year
winter would last longer in India
hard.why: Without the tilt, sunlight would fall the same way all year, so there would be no seasons.

hard.q: A total solar eclipse is seen only from a narrow strip of Earth because
o: the Moon is larger than Earth
the Moon's dark shadow on Earth is small
eclipses happen only at the poles
hard.why: The Moon's darkest shadow is a small spot on Earth, so only a narrow strip sees totality.

hard.q: The smaller Moon can fully cover the Sun because
o: the Moon is larger than the Sun
the Sun is dimmer than the Moon
the Moon is much closer to Earth than the Sun is
the Moon is made of a dark material
hard.why: The Moon is much closer to us than the Sun, so it appears about the same size and can cover it.

hard.q: In June, days in the northern hemisphere are longer because
o: Earth is nearer to the Sun in June
the northern hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun
the Sun moves around the Earth
the Moon pulls sunlight to India
hard.why: The northern hemisphere tilted towards the Sun gets more hours of daylight.

hard.q: When it is summer in India (northern hemisphere) the southern hemisphere
o: also has summer, getting the same light
has winter because it is tilted away from the Sun
hard.why: When the northern hemisphere tilts towards the Sun, the southern hemisphere tilts away and has winter.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: She ___ in Pune since 2019.
easy.why: 'Since' needs present perfect.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: I ___ my homework before dinner yesterday.
easy.why: Past perfect for the earlier action.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: They ___ a movie when the power went off.
easy.why: Past continuous interrupted by a past event.

easy.q: Choose the past participle of 'take'.
easy.why: Take - took - taken.

easy.q: Choose the past participle of 'write'.
easy.why: Write - wrote - written.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: By next year, I ___ school.
easy.why: Future perfect with 'by next year'.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: How long ___ you ___ here?
medium.why: Present perfect continuous for an action still going on.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: After she ___ the letter, she cried.
medium.why: Past perfect with 'after' for the first action.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: He ___ the door before the thief entered.
medium.why: Past perfect for the earlier action.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: If I had money, I ___ a car.
medium.why: Second conditional: would + base verb.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: If it rains, we ___ indoors.
medium.why: First conditional: present in if, will in result.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: I ___ the news when you called.
medium.why: An action in progress was interrupted.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: If she had studied harder, she would have passed.
If she studied harder, she would have passed yesterday.
If she had studied harder, she will pass.
If she has studied, she would have passed.
hard.why: Third conditional: had + participle; would have + participle.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: No sooner he had left than it started to rain.
No sooner had he left then it started to rain.
No sooner had he left than it started to rain.
No sooner he left when it started to rain.
hard.why: 'No sooner had ... than'.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: I have been waiting since morning.
I was waiting since morning now.
hard.why: 'Since' with an action still going needs the perfect continuous.

hard.q: Which sentence uses the verb form correctly?
o: The glass was broken by the child.
The glass was broke by the child.
The glass was breaked by the child.
The glass has broke by the child.
hard.why: Passive uses the past participle: broken.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: She said she has finished the work yesterday.
She says she had finished work tomorrow.
She said she will finished the work.
She said she had finished the work.
hard.why: Past reporting verb, past perfect for an earlier action.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: I wish I studied more last year.
I wish I had studied more.
I wish I have studied more.
I wish I would studied more.
hard.why: A wish about the past uses past perfect.

easy.q: Choose the verb: The children ___ playing in the garden.
easy.why: Plural children: are.

easy.q: Choose the verb: Mohit and his sister ___ here.
easy.why: Two subjects joined by and.

easy.q: Choose the verb: Nobody ___ the answer.
easy.why: Nobody is singular.

easy.q: Choose the verb: The pair of shoes ___ new.
easy.why: The subject is 'pair'.

easy.q: Choose the verb: The class ___ a test today. (acting as one unit)
easy.why: The class as a unit takes a singular verb.

easy.q: Choose the verb: Two kilos of sugar ___ enough.
easy.why: A quantity as a whole is singular.

medium.q: Choose the verb: Neither the boys nor the girl ___ ready.
medium.why: Verb agrees with the nearer subject: girl.

medium.q: Choose the verb: The number of players ___ eleven.
medium.why: 'The number of' is singular.

medium.q: Choose the verb: The poet and writer ___ honoured. (one person)
medium.why: One person: singular.

medium.q: Choose the verb: Economics ___ taught in Class 11.
medium.why: Subjects ending in -ics are singular.

medium.q: Choose the verb: A number of guests ___ arrived.
medium.why: 'A number of' means many: plural.

medium.q: Choose the verb: Each of the cars ___ a number plate.
medium.why: Each is singular.

hard.q: Choose the verb: Not only the captain but also the players ___ tired.
hard.why: Agrees with the nearer subject, players.

hard.q: Choose the verb: One of the books I bought ___ torn.
hard.why: The subject is 'one'.

hard.q: Choose the verb: The principal, with all his teachers, ___ attending the event.
hard.why: With does not make the subject plural.

hard.q: Choose the verb: Cattle ___ grazing in the field.
hard.why: Cattle is a plural noun.

hard.q: Choose the verb: Either of the two answers ___ correct.
hard.why: Either is singular.

hard.q: Choose the verb: There ___ many reasons for his absence.
hard.why: The real subject 'reasons' is plural.

easy.q: Change to passive: Rita bakes cakes.
easy.why: Simple present: are + participle.

easy.q: Change to passive: Dad will paint the gate.
o: The gate was painted by Dad.
The gate will paint by Dad.
The gate will be painted by Dad.
The gate is painted by Dad.
easy.why: Simple future: will be + participle.

easy.q: Change to passive: The boys broke the window.
o: The window is broken by the boys.
The window was broken by the boys.
The window broke by the boys.
The window was breaking by the boys.
easy.why: Simple past: was + participle.

easy.q: Change to passive: She writes a diary.
o: A diary is written by her.
A diary was written by her.
A diary is writing by her.
easy.why: Simple present passive.

easy.q: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
o: The cake was eaten by the guests.
easy.why: The cake receives the action.

easy.q: Change to passive: Priya opened the gift.
o: The gift is opened by Priya.
The gift was opened by Priya.
The gift was open by Priya.
easy.why: Simple past passive.

medium.q: Change to passive: The cook is preparing dinner.
o: Dinner is prepared by the cook.
Dinner was being prepared by the cook.
Dinner is being prepared by the cook.
Dinner has been prepared by the cook.
medium.why: Present continuous passive: is being + participle.

medium.q: Change to passive: They had finished the game.
o: The game had been finished by them.
The game has been finished by them.
The game was finished by them.
The game had finished by them.
medium.why: Past perfect passive.

medium.q: Change to passive: He has solved the puzzle.
o: The puzzle is solved by him.
The puzzle was solved by him.
The puzzle had been solved by him.
The puzzle has been solved by him.
medium.why: Present perfect passive.

medium.q: Change to passive: Who has broken the glass?
o: Who has the glass been broken?
By whom the glass was broken?
By whom has the glass been broken?
medium.why: Present perfect interrogative passive.

medium.q: Change to passive: You should obey the rules.
o: The rules should obey by you.
The rules should be obeyed by you.
The rules should have obeyed by you.
medium.why: Modal passive: should be + participle.

medium.q: Change to passive: Does she sing the song?
o: Does the song sung by her?
Is the song sing by her?
Was the song sung by her?
Is the song sung by her?
medium.why: Simple present question passive.

hard.q: Change to passive: Open the window.
hard.why: An imperative becomes 'Let ... be + participle'.

hard.q: Which sentence has the correct passive?
o: I taught English by my aunt.
English was taught me by my aunt was.
I was taught English by my aunt.
I am teaching English by my aunt.
hard.why: With two objects, 'I was taught' is natural.

hard.q: Change to passive: People believe that he is rich.
o: He is believing to be rich.
He is believed to be rich.
It is believe that he is rich.
hard.why: Impersonal passive with infinitive.

hard.q: Change to passive: She is going to write a report.
o: A report is going to be written by her.
A report is going to write by her.
A report was going to be written by her.
A report will write by her.
hard.why: Be going to: is going to be + participle.

hard.q: Which sentence cannot be turned into the passive?
hard.why: Sleep is intransitive; it takes no object.

hard.q: Change to passive: They are laughing at him.
o: He is laughed at by them.
He is being laughed at by them.
He was being laughed at by them.
He is laughing at by them.
hard.why: The preposition stays after the verb.

easy.q: Change to reported speech: He said, "I am happy."
o: He said that I am happy.
He said that he is happy.
He said that he was happy.
He told that he was happy.
easy.why: Present becomes past in reporting; I becomes he.

easy.q: Change to reported speech: Ravi said, "I will come."
o: Ravi said that he would come.
Ravi said that he will come.
Ravi said that I would come.
easy.why: Will becomes would.

easy.q: Change to reported speech: She said, "I like tea."
o: She said that she likes tea.
She said that she had liked tea.
She said that she liked tea.
easy.why: Simple present becomes simple past.

easy.q: Change 'here' in reported speech:
easy.why: Here becomes there.

easy.q: Change 'today' in reported speech after a past reporting verb:
easy.why: Today becomes that day.

easy.q: Change 'now' in reported speech:
easy.why: Now becomes then.

medium.q: Change to reported speech: He said, "I am reading a book."
o: He said that he was reading a book.
He said that he is reading a book.
He said that he read a book.
He said that I was reading a book.
medium.why: Present continuous becomes past continuous.

medium.q: Change to reported speech: He said to me, "Where do you live?"
o: He asked me where do I live.
He said me where I lived.
He asked me where I lived.
He asked me that where I lived.
medium.why: A question becomes a statement order with 'asked'.

medium.q: Change to reported speech: She said, "I have finished."
o: She said that she has finished.
She said that she had finished.
She said that I had finished.
medium.why: Present perfect becomes past perfect.

medium.q: Change to reported speech: The teacher said, "Sit down."
o: The teacher told them to sit down.
The teacher said them to sit down.
The teacher told that sit down.
medium.why: A command uses 'told ... to'.

medium.q: Change to reported speech: She said to him, "Do you know the way?"
o: She asked him do he know the way.
She said him if he knew the way.
She asked him that he knew the way.
She asked him if he knew the way.
medium.why: Yes/no question uses if or whether.

medium.q: Change to reported speech: He said to us, "Please help me."
o: He requested us to help him.
He said that please help him.
medium.why: Please shows a request.

hard.q: Change to reported speech: She said, "I saw him yesterday."
o: She said that she saw him yesterday.
She said that she has seen him the previous day.
She said that she had seen him the day before.
She said that I had seen him the day before.
hard.why: Yesterday becomes the day before; simple past becomes past perfect.

hard.q: Change to reported speech: Mother said, "The sun rises in the east."
o: Mother said that the sun rises in the east.
Mother said that the sun rose in the east not.
Mother said that the sun had risen.
Mother said the sun will rise.
hard.why: A universal truth keeps its tense.

hard.q: Change to reported speech: He said, "I will come tomorrow."
o: He said that he will come tomorrow.
He said that he came tomorrow.
He said that I would come the next day.
He said that he would come the next day.
hard.why: Tomorrow becomes the next day.

hard.q: Change to reported speech: He said, "What a lovely day!"
o: He asked what a lovely day.
He said what a lovely day.
He exclaimed that it was a lovely day.
He exclaimed what a lovely day was.
hard.why: An exclamation uses exclaimed (with joy).

hard.q: Change to reported speech: "Let us go to the park," said Rita.
o: Rita ordered that they go to the park.
Rita suggested that they go to the park.
Rita said that let us go to the park.
Rita asked what they go to the park.
hard.why: 'Let us' is a suggestion.

hard.q: Change to reported speech: The boy said, "Alas! I have failed."
o: The boy said alas that he failed.
The boy said with joy that he had failed.

easy.q: Choose the conjunction: I will go ___ you come.

easy.q: Choose the relative pronoun: This is the book ___ I read.
easy.why: That refers to a thing.

easy.q: Choose the conjunction: Wash your hands ___ you eat.
easy.why: Before shows time order.

easy.q: Choose the conjunction: He is poor ___ honest.
easy.why: But shows contrast.

easy.why: Until marks the time limit.

medium.why: Whose shows possession.

medium.q: Choose the conjunction: ___ it rained, the match went on.
medium.why: Although shows contrast.

medium.q: Which is the subordinate clause? 'He stayed home because he was ill.'

medium.q: Choose the conjunction: Hurry up, ___ we will be late.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: If I were rich, I would travel the world.
If I was rich, I will travel the world.
If I am rich, I would travel the world.
If I were rich, I will travel the world.
hard.why: Second conditional uses were and would.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: Not only he sang, but he also danced.
Not only did he sang, but also danced he.
Not only did he sing, but he also danced.
Not only he did sing, but danced.
hard.why: Inversion follows 'Not only' at the start.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: Unless you don't work hard, you will fail.
Unless you work hard, you will fail.
Unless you will work hard, you fail.
Unless you worked hard, you will fail.
hard.why: Unless already carries the negative idea.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: This is the boy whom I met yesterday.
This is the boy whom met me yesterday.
This is the boy which I met yesterday.
This is the boy whose I met yesterday.
hard.why: Whom is the object of 'met'.

hard.q: Which sentence has a noun clause?
o: The girl who sang is my sister.
I know that she is honest.
hard.why: 'that she is honest' is the object of know.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: Hardly she had left when the phone rang.
Hardly had she left when the phone rang.
Hardly had she left than the phone rang.
Hardly she left when the phone rang.
hard.why: 'Hardly had ... when'.

easy.q: Choose the word: She is fond ___ music.

easy.q: Choose the word: The cat jumped ___ the table.

o: I like apples oranges, and bananas
I like, apples oranges and bananas.
I like apples, oranges, and, bananas.
I like apples, oranges and bananas.

easy.q: Which of these numbers cannot be a perfect square?
easy.why: A perfect square never ends in 2, 3, 7 or 8, and 2038 ends in 8.

easy.q: What is the cube root of 2744?
What is the value of 35 squared?
easy.why: 35^2 = 3 x 4 x 100 + 25 = 1225 (n5 squared ends in 25).

easy.q: What is the smallest number by which 12 must be multiplied to get a perfect square?
easy.why: 12 = 2 x 2 x 3, and the lone 3 needs a partner, so multiply by 3 to get 36.

easy.q: How many whole numbers lie strictly between 12^2 and 13^2?
easy.why: Between n^2 and (n+1)^2 there are 2n numbers, so 2 x 12 = 24.

easy.q: What is the last digit of 27 cubed?
easy.why: Only the last digit matters: 7 x 7 x 7 = 343 ends in 3.

medium.q: What is the sum of the first 15 odd numbers?

What is the smallest perfect square divisible by 6, 8 and 10?
medium.why: LCM = 120 = 2^3 x 3 x 5. Make every power even: 2^4 x 3^2 x 5^2 = 3600.

medium.q: What is the smallest number by which 252 must be multiplied to get a perfect square?
medium.why: 252 = 2^2 x 3^2 x 7. Only the 7 is unpaired.

medium.q: A square floor measures 30 tiles by 30 tiles. How many tiles are in the single outer border row?
medium.why: Border = 30^2 - 28^2 = 900 - 784 = 116. Counting 4 x 30 double-counts the 4 corners.

medium.q: What is 10 cubed minus 9 cubed?

hard.q: How many perfect squares lie between 200 and 1000?

hard.why: A cube ending in 8 has a root ending in 2. 12^3 = 1728 has 4 digits; 22^3 = 10648 has 5.

hard.q: 5 x 6 x 7 x 8 + 1 is the square of which number?
hard.why: 1680 + 1 = 1681 = 41 x 41. Product of 4 consecutive numbers plus 1 is a square.

hard.q: What is the smallest number greater than 1 that is both a perfect square and a perfect cube?
hard.why: It needs every prime power divisible by 6. The smallest is 2^6 = 64.

hard.q: How many two-digit numbers have a square ending in the digit 9?
hard.why: The number must end in 3 or 7: 9 tens digits x 2 endings = 18.
The sum of the first n cubes is (1+2+...+n)^2 = 55^2 = 3025.

easy.q: How is 45,000 written in scientific notation?

easy.q: What is 5^6 divided by 5^2?
easy.why: Same base: subtract exponents, 6 - 2 = 4.

easy.why: Any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1, so 1 + 1 = 2.

medium.q: Simplify (3^2)^4.
medium.why: Power of a power: multiply exponents, 2 x 4 = 8.

medium.q: What is the value of (1/2)^-3?

medium.topic: Powers of ten and negative exponents

easy.q: A quadrilateral has all four sides equal but its angles are not right angles. What is it?

easy.why: A diagonal splits it into 2 triangles of 180 degrees each.

easy.q: Which is always true for the diagonals of a rectangle?
o: They do not bisect each other
They are equal and bisect each other
easy.why: Rectangle diagonals are equal and bisect each other. Perpendicular diagonals belong to a rhombus.

easy.why: Diagonals meet at right angles and bisect: side = square root of 6^2 + 8^2 = 10.

easy.q: One angle of a parallelogram is 70 degrees. What is an adjacent angle?
easy.why: Adjacent angles of a parallelogram add to 180 degrees.

medium.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio 1:2:3:4. What is the largest angle?
medium.why: One part = 360 / 10 = 36, so the largest is 4 x 36 = 144.

medium.q: Which statement is true?
medium.why: A square has four equal sides, so it is a rhombus, but not the other way round.

medium.q: A rectangle has perimeter 36 cm and its length is twice its breadth. What is the breadth?
medium.why: 2(2b + b) = 36 gives b = 6.

medium.q: In a parallelogram one angle is three times its adjacent angle. What is the smallest angle?
In trapezium ABCD, AB is parallel to CD, angle A = 72 and angle B = 85 degrees. What is angle C + angle D?
medium.why: Angle D = 180 - 72 = 108 and angle C = 180 - 85 = 95. Sum = 203.

medium.q: A rhombus has side 8 cm and one angle of 60 degrees. What is its shorter diagonal?
medium.why: The shorter diagonal makes an equilateral triangle with two sides, so it is 8.

hard.q: What is the angle between the bisectors of two adjacent angles of a parallelogram?
hard.why: Half of 180 is 90, so in the triangle formed the third angle is 90.

hard.q: A rhombus has perimeter 52 cm and one diagonal of 24 cm. What is the other diagonal?
hard.why: Side 13, half-diagonal 12, so other half = square root of 169 - 144 = 5; the diagonal is 10.

hard.q: A parallelogram has equal diagonals. What must it be?
hard.why: A parallelogram with equal diagonals has right angles, so it is a rectangle.

hard.q: In rectangle ABCD the diagonals meet at O and angle AOB = 64 degrees. What is angle OAB?
hard.why: OA = OB, so the base angles are (180 - 64) / 2 = 58.

hard.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are x, x+10, x+20 and x+30 degrees. What is the largest angle?
hard.why: 4x + 60 = 360 gives x = 75, so the largest is 105.

hard.q: What shape do you get by joining the midpoints of the sides of a rectangle that is not a square?
hard.why: All four joining segments are half a diagonal, so equal; the diagonals are not equal, so it is not a square.

easy.q: The sum of three odd numbers is always...
easy.why: Odd + odd = even, and even + odd = odd.

easy.q: Which of these numbers is divisible by 9?

easy.q: What is the remainder when 47 is divided by 5?
Which of these numbers is divisible by 6?
easy.why: 4236 is even and its digit sum 15 is a multiple of 3.

easy.q: 23 leaves remainder 3 and 34 leaves remainder 4 when divided by 5. What remainder does 23 + 34 leave?

medium.why: Numbers are 12k + 2: 2, 14, 26...

medium.q: n x n + n is always...

medium.q: What remainder does 123 x 456 leave when divided by 5?

hard.why: Among three consecutive numbers there is a multiple of 2 and of 3, but not always of 4 or 9.

What is the smallest number that leaves remainder 4 on division by 9 and remainder 5 on division by 7?
The difference between a two-digit number and its reversal is always divisible by...

hard.why: 9(b - a) = 27 gives b - a = 3, and a + b = 11 gives a = 4, b = 7.

A rectangle is 9 cm by 12 cm. What is its diagonal?

medium.q: Two friends leave a spot. One walks 9 km east and the other 12 km north. How far apart are they?

Using (2n+1, 2n^2+2n, 2n^2+2n+1), what is the largest number of the triple whose smallest is 11?
Which of these triples is primitive (cannot be reduced to a smaller triple)?

easy.q: Which pair of quantities varies inversely?

Speed and time for a fixed distance
Distance and time at constant speed
easy.why: If speed doubles, the time halves.

easy.q: A tap fills a tank in 6 hours. What fraction does it fill in 1 hour?
easy.why: One hour is one sixth of the time.

easy.q: 6 workers finish a job in 10 days. How many days do 12 workers take?
easy.why: Twice the workers, half the time.

easy.q: In a pie chart, what angle does a 25% sector have?
x and y are inversely proportional. When x = 4, y = 15. What is y when x = 6?
A can finish a job in 10 days. What fraction of it does he finish in 4 days?

medium.q: 8 men build a wall in 15 days. How long do 10 men take?
medium.why: 8 x 15 = 120 man-days, divided by 10.

medium.q: Food for 40 students lasts 12 days. How long does it last for 60 students?
medium.why: 480 student-days / 60.

medium.q: In a survey of 180 students, 54 choose football. What is its sector angle?
5 workers finish a job in 12 days. How many workers are needed to finish it in 4 days?
medium.why: 60 worker-days / 4.

medium.q: A car at 60 km/h takes 4 hours for a trip. How long at 80 km/h?
medium.why: Distance 240 km / 80.

medium.q: A can finish a job in 6 days and B in 3 days. How long do they take together?

hard.q: 12 workers finish a job in 15 days. How many extra workers are needed to finish it in 9 days?
hard.why: 180 worker-days / 9 = 20 workers, so 8 more.

hard.q: Pipe A fills a tank in 12 hours and pipe B in 8 hours. How long do they take together?
A family's monthly budget of Rs 48,000 is drawn as a pie chart. Savings take 150 degrees. How much is saved?
Pipe A fills a tank in 6 hours and an outlet empties it in 10 hours. With both open, how long to fill the tank?
A and B together finish a job in 12 days. A alone takes 20 days. How long does B alone take?
Food for 30 students lasts 20 days. After 5 days, 10 more students join. How many more days will the food last?

easy.q: In the Sierpinski triangle, stage 1 has 3 filled triangles. How many are there at stage 2?

easy.why: A cube has 6 faces.

easy.q: A 3 x 3 x 3 cube is built from unit cubes. How many unit cubes is that?
How many edges does a cube have?

medium.q: How many filled triangles does the Sierpinski triangle have at stage 4?

A tower on a 2 x 2 base has column heights 3, 2, 1 and 2. How many cubes in all?
How many polygons make the net of a triangular prism?
medium.why: 2 triangles and 3 rectangles.

medium.q: A unit square has its middle ninth removed. The same is done to each of the 8 remaining squares. What area is left?
A solid has a 3 x 3 bottom layer, a 2 x 2 layer above, and one cube on top. How many cubes in all?

hard.q: How many different nets does a cube have, if rotations and flips are treated as the same?
hard.why: There are exactly 11.

hard.q: Heights of columns on a 3 x 3 base are, row by row: 3,1,2 / 1,1,1 / 2,0,1. How many cubes are there?

A 4 x 4 x 4 cube is painted outside and cut into 64 unit cubes. How many have exactly one face painted?

hard.q: A 5 x 5 x 5 cube is built from unit cubes. How many cubes are not on the surface?
hard.why: Inner 3 x 3 x 3.

What is the median of 3, 9, 5, 7, 1?
Which display is best to show how temperature changed over a week?
easy.why: Line graphs show change over time.

easy.q: The mean of 5 numbers is 12. What is their sum?
Temperatures Mon to Fri are 28, 30, 29, 31, 32. What is the biggest rise from one day to the next?
easy.why: 28 to 30 and 29 to 31 are rises of 2.

easy.q: What is the median of 12, 15, 11, 18, 14?

medium.q: The mean of 6 numbers is 15. When one number, 10, is removed, what is the mean of the rest?
medium.why: 90 - 10 = 80, divided by 5.

medium.q: The mean of 8 scores is 72. Two more scores, 80 and 90, are added. What is the new mean?
In the data 4, 8, 10, 14, 20, the 20 is replaced by 200. What happens?
o: The mean changes, the median stays 10
medium.why: The middle value is still 10.

medium.q: Every one of 20 readings was recorded 2 too high and the mean came out as 50. What is the true mean?
medium.why: Mean shifts by the same 2.

medium.q: For that rainfall data, what is the difference between the wettest and driest month?
Number of siblings: 0 (3 students), 1 (5), 2 (4), 3 (2). What is the median?
medium.why: 14 students; the 7th and 8th values are both 1.

hard.q: Six values have median 15. The two middle values are 12 and x. What is x?

The mean of 5 numbers is 20. When one is removed, the mean of the rest is 18. Which was removed?
Class A has 25 students with mean 40. Class B has 15 with mean 48. What is the combined mean?
30 students average 60. 20 of them average 55. What is the average of the other 10?
Seven values in order have median 20. The smallest value is replaced by 100. What is the new median?

easy.q: A two-digit number has tens digit a and units digit b. How do you write its reversal?
easy.why: The old units digit now sits in the tens place.

easy.q: Solve x + 7 = 15.
easy.why: Subtract 7.

easy.q: The nth term of a pattern is 3n. What is the 10th term?

n squares in a row need 3n + 1 matchsticks. How many for 6 squares?
What is 10a + b added to its reversal?
easy.why: Add 10a + b and 10b + a.

medium.q: Think of n, multiply by 3, add 12, divide by 3 and subtract n. What is the result?

A father is 3 times his son's age. In 10 years the sum of their ages will be 80. How old is the son now?
The nth term of a pattern is 5n - 2. What is the 12th term?
A cart sells 40 dosas for a total profit of Rs 800. Each dosa costs Rs 30 to make. What is the selling price?
Add all three rotations of the digits 3, 4, 5: 345, 453 and 534. What is the sum?

hard.q: Three consecutive even numbers add up to 114. What is the middle number?
Two pens and three notebooks cost Rs 75. A notebook costs Rs 5 more than a pen. What does a notebook cost?
Step n of a tile pattern has (n + 2)^2 - 4 tiles. Which simplified expression is the same?
For every odd number n, n^2 - 1 is divisible by...

hard.q: A pilgrim's flowers double at each of two ponds. After each pond she offers 16 flowers at a shrine and ends with none. How many did she start with?
hard.why: Work backwards: before the last offering 16, before doubling 8; add the first 16 to get 24, halve to get 12.

hard.q: A four-row pyramid has base 2, 1, 3, 2, and each cell is the sum of the two below. What is the top?
hard.why: 3,4,5 then 7,9 then 16.

easy.q: What is the area of a rectangle 14 m by 9 m?

A square park's side is doubled. Its area becomes...

medium.q: A garden is 20 m by 15 m. A 2 m wide path runs inside all around it. What is the area of the path?

A frame measures 30 cm by 20 cm outside, with a border 3 cm wide. What is the area of the border?
A parallelogram has sides 12 cm and 8 cm, and the height on the 12 cm side is 6 cm. What is the height on the 8 cm side?

medium.q: A right triangle has legs 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the height drawn to the hypotenuse?
medium.why: Area 24 = 1/2 x 10 x h.

medium.q: Joining the midpoints of the sides of a triangle makes a smaller triangle. What fraction of the original area is it?
medium.why: It is a scale of 1/2, so area 1/4.

hard.q: A rhombus has diagonals 16 cm and 30 cm. What is its area?

hard.q: A path 3 m wide runs round the outside of a 50 m by 40 m field. What is the area of the path?
A triangle PQR has PQ = PR = 10 cm and QR = 12 cm. What is its area?
hard.why: Height = 8.

hard.q: P is the midpoint of AB in parallelogram ABCD of area 80 square cm. What is the area of triangle PCD?
hard.why: Same base CD and height as the parallelogram, so half.

hard.q: The midpoints of the sides of a square of side 12 cm are joined. What is the area of the inner square?
hard.why: Half the area of 144.

easy.q: A scientific model is best described as:
o: an exact full-size copy of the real object
a simplified picture of something that keeps the important features and leaves out minor details
a guess that no one has tested
a law that can never change
easy.why: A model keeps what matters for the question and drops the rest, so the problem becomes easier to study.

easy.q: In physics, the symbol c stands for:
o: the speed of sound in air
the speed of light in vacuum
easy.why: The symbol c stands for the speed of light, about 3 x 10^8 m/s.

easy.q: The SI unit of mass is the:
easy.why: The SI base unit of mass is the kilogram.

easy.q: How many minutes are there in 2 days?
easy.why: 1 day = 24 x 60 = 1440 minutes, so 2 days = 2880 minutes.

easy.q: A statement about what will happen under given conditions, which can later be checked, is called a:
easy.why: Predictions can be tested against what is later observed.

easy.q: A statement that describes a regular pattern in nature, often written as an equation, is called a:
easy.why: A law describes what happens in nature in a regular way.

medium.q: To estimate how long a cricket ball takes to fall from a 20 m high roof, which detail can be safely ignored in a simple model?
o: the logo printed on the ball
the starting speed of the ball
medium.why: Height, gravity and starting speed affect the fall time; a printed logo does not.

medium.q: Anita breathes 15 times a minute, taking in about 0.5 L each time. How many litres of air does she breathe in one hour?
medium.why: 15 x 60 = 900 breaths; 900 x 0.5 L = 450 L. 900 L forgets the 0.5 L per breath.

medium.q: Which statement correctly contrasts a law and a theory?
o: A law describes what happens; a theory explains why it happens
A law is a guess; a theory is a proven fact
A theory is always simpler than a law
A law and a theory mean exactly the same
medium.why: Laws describe patterns; theories are tested explanations of why they occur.

medium.q: Speed = distance / time. If a bus covers twice the distance in the same time, its speed:
medium.why: Speed is proportional to distance when time is fixed, so doubling distance doubles speed.

medium.q: Which of these is a testable prediction?
o: This plant is a happy plant
If I water this plant with 100 mL daily, it will grow at least 2 cm in a week
medium.why: A testable prediction states a measurable result under stated conditions.

medium.q: A model predicts that a pendulum swings once in 2.0 s, but you measure 2.3 s. What should you do first?
o: Change the measured value to 2.0 s
Decide that science does not work
Recheck the measurement and the assumptions, such as ignoring air drag
medium.why: Mismatches are clues: check data and assumptions, then improve the model.

hard.q: A person breathes 16 times a minute, about 0.5 L per breath. About how many litres of air is that in one day?
A heart beats 72 times a minute. How many beats are there in one day?
hard.why: 72 x 60 x 24 = 103,680. 4,320 is beats in an hour.

hard.q: A classmate says, "A theory is just a guess." The best reply is:
o: Yes, theories are guesses that no one tests
A scientific theory is a well-tested explanation backed by a lot of evidence
A theory is a law that has been proven wrong
A theory is a number with units
hard.why: In science a theory explains many observations and has survived many tests.

hard.q: Light travels 3 x 10^8 m/s. The Sun is 1.5 x 10^11 m away. About how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
hard.why: Time = 1.5 x 10^11 / 3 x 10^8 = 500 s, which is about 8.3 minutes.

hard.q: Scientists may treat a cow as a sphere to estimate heat loss. Why is this acceptable?
o: Models must include every detail to be valid
It proves that shape never matters
It keeps only the features that matter for that question, and answers hold within those assumptions
hard.why: A simple model gives useful estimates if its limits are remembered.

hard.q: Someone says food cooked during a solar eclipse is poisonous. What is the most scientific way to check?
o: Compare food cooked during and outside an eclipse under the same conditions and look at the evidence
Believe it because elders say so
Reject it without looking at any evidence
Count how many people believe it
hard.why: Claims are tested with controlled comparisons and evidence.

easy.q: Who first observed cells, using a thin slice of cork?
easy.why: Hooke saw the box-like compartments of cork in 1665 and named them cells.

easy.q: Which organelle is called the powerhouse of the cell?
easy.why: Mitochondria release energy as ATP.

easy.q: The main material of the plant cell wall is:
easy.why: Plant cell walls are made mainly of cellulose.
easy.topic: Cell membrane, cell wall and osmosis

easy.q: Protein synthesis takes place on:
easy.why: Ribosomes build proteins.

easy.q: Osmosis is the movement of:
o: salt across a membrane from concentrated to dilute solution
water across a selectively permeable membrane from dilute to concentrated solution
water from concentrated to dilute solution
easy.why: Water moves toward the region with more dissolved substances.
easy.topic: Cell membrane, cell wall and osmosis

easy.q: A bacterium differs from an onion cell because it does not have a:
easy.why: Prokaryotes have DNA but no membrane-bound nucleus.

medium.q: Dry raisins soaked in plain water swell up because:
o: the raisin cells make more water
the cell wall pumps in sugar
water enters the raisin cells by osmosis
medium.why: The cell sap is more concentrated than plain water, so water moves in.
medium.topic: Cell membrane, cell wall and osmosis

medium.q: Which statement about endoplasmic reticulum is correct?
o: SER has no ribosomes and helps make lipids; RER has ribosomes and helps make proteins
SER is studded with ribosomes and makes proteins
medium.why: Ribosomes give RER its rough look.

medium.q: A plant cell kept in strong salt solution loses water and its membrane pulls away from the wall. This is called:
medium.why: Plasmolysis is shrinking of the protoplast in a hypertonic solution.
medium.topic: Cell membrane, cell wall and osmosis

medium.q: Mature human red blood cells have no nucleus. A result of this is that they:
o: make their own proteins in the nucleus
cannot divide or repair themselves but have more room for haemoglobin
medium.why: Losing the nucleus makes space for haemoglobin.

medium.q: If all mitochondria are removed from an animal cell, the cell would:
o: make much less ATP and soon run short of energy
medium.why: Mitochondria are the main source of ATP.

medium.q: The correct path of a protein made for secretion is:
o: ribosome on RER, then Golgi apparatus, then vesicle to the membrane
medium.why: Proteins are made, modified and packed in that order.

hard.q: Amla pieces kept in salt and sugar do not spoil. The main reason is that:
o: salt and sugar draw water out of microbes by osmosis, so they cannot grow
salt and sugar kill all cells by heat
salt makes the amla acidic only
hard.why: Strongly concentrated surroundings dehydrate microbes.
hard.topic: Cell membrane, cell wall and osmosis

hard.q: A human body cell has 46 chromosomes. If gametes were made by mitosis, a zygote would have:
hard.why: Each gamete would have 46, so the zygote would have 92. Meiosis prevents this.

hard.q: Which statement is true of both mitochondria and chloroplasts?
o: Both make glucose from carbon dioxide
Both are found in every cell
Both have a double membrane and their own DNA
hard.why: They are double-membraned organelles with their own DNA.

hard.q: In a potato-cup experiment, a boiled potato cup with sugar in it shows no rise in water level. The reason is that boiling:
o: turned water into gas inside the cup
destroyed the selectively permeable membrane of the cells
hard.why: Dead cells lose selective permeability, so osmosis stops.
hard.topic: Cell membrane, cell wall and osmosis

hard.q: A cell with 8 chromosomes undergoes meiosis. The result is:
hard.why: Meiosis gives four haploid cells.

hard.q: In a culture, normal cells stop dividing when they touch each other, but some cells keep piling up. These cells have most likely lost:
hard.why: Loss of contact inhibition leads to uncontrolled growth, as in tumours.

easy.q: Growth in the length of a root or shoot tip is due to:
easy.why: Apical meristem at tips makes the plant longer.

easy.q: The tissue that carries food from leaves to other parts of a plant is:
easy.why: Phloem carries prepared food; xylem carries water.

easy.q: The tissue that lines the mouth and the inside of the gut is:
easy.why: Epithelia cover surfaces and line cavities.

easy.q: A tendon joins:
easy.why: Ligaments join bone to bone; tendons join muscle to bone.

easy.q: The knee is an example of a:
easy.why: Knees bend and straighten like a door hinge.

easy.q: Messages are carried through the body by:
easy.why: Nerve cells carry signals.

medium.q: Meristematic cells usually have:
o: thin walls, dense cytoplasm and little or no vacuole
thick walls and a large vacuole
medium.why: These features suit rapidly dividing cells.

medium.q: Grass grows back quickly after mowing because of:
o: apical meristem in the root tip
intercalary meristem at the base of leaves
medium.why: Intercalary meristem lies at bases of leaves or internodes.

medium.q: The hard shell of a coconut husk gets its strength from:
medium.why: Sclerenchyma has thick lignified walls.

medium.q: Which tissue gives tender stems and leaf stalks both flexibility and support?
medium.why: Collenchyma has unevenly thickened walls that bend.

medium.q: A ring of bark is cut all around a tree trunk. Soon the roots below the cut starve because:
o: food cannot move down through the removed phloem
water cannot go up through the bark
leaves stop making sugar at once
medium.why: Phloem lies in the bark and carries food downward.

medium.q: An involuntary, unstriped muscle found in the walls of the intestine is:
medium.why: Smooth muscle moves food without conscious control.

hard.q: The tip of a growing root, about 2 mm, is cut off. Which result is most likely?
o: The root grows twice as fast
The root stops growing longer because its apical meristem is lost
hard.why: Apical meristem at the tip gives length growth.

hard.q: A trunk's girth grows 3 cm each year. At 10 years it measures 60 cm. Assuming the same rate, its girth at 15 years will be:
hard.why: Five more years add 15 cm. Lateral meristem increases girth.

hard.q: A ring of bark is removed from a tree. Leaves stay green for some days. Why?
o: Xylem inside still carries water up, while the phloem that carried food down is gone
hard.why: Xylem lies deeper than bark.

hard.q: Which statement is correct?
o: Xylem has dead vessels and tracheids as well as living xylem parenchyma
hard.why: Plant tissues can be complex and mixed.

hard.q: Which pairing of tissue and function is correct?
o: Companion cell: helps the sieve tube
hard.why: Companion cells keep sieve tube members alive.

hard.q: Landing on stiff legs hurts more than landing with bent knees because:
o: joints cannot bend, so the force acts for a shorter time and is larger
hard.why: Bending lengthens the stopping time.

easy.q: Meera walks 300 m from home to school and returns the same way. Her displacement is:
easy.why: She ends where she began, so displacement is zero (distance is 600 m).

easy.q: 72 km/h expressed in m/s is:
A car at 10 m/s speeds up at 2 m/s^2 for 5 s. Its final speed is:
A train covers 150 km in 3 hours. Its average speed is:
Acceleration is the rate of change of:
easy.why: a = change in velocity / time.

easy.q: The slope of a position-time graph gives:
easy.why: Slope = change in position / time = velocity.

medium.q: A car starts from rest with a = 3 m/s^2. Distance covered in 6 s is:
A bike at 20 m/s brakes uniformly to rest in 4 s. Distance covered while braking is:

medium.why: Average speed 12.5 m/s x 10 s = 125 m.

medium.q: A swimmer does 2 lengths of a 50 m pool in 100 s and ends at the start. Average speed and average velocity are:
medium.why: Distance 100 m in 100 s; net displacement zero.

medium.q: A scooter moves at a steady 40 km/h around a curve. It is accelerating because:
o: its direction, and so its velocity, changes
medium.why: Velocity includes direction.

medium.q: A body speeds up uniformly from 0 to 12 m/s in 6 s, then moves at 12 m/s for 4 s. Total distance is:

hard.q: A bus at 20 m/s sees an obstacle 55 m ahead. Reaction time is 0.5 s, then it brakes at 5 m/s^2. It stops:

hard.q: The tip of a 14 cm minute hand moves from 6:00 to 6:30 (use pi = 22/7). Distance and displacement of the tip are:
